Hi team, 

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount. 


Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Cheers,
Afiba

Internal summary (copied from the Main Ticket):

{quote}We're considering a partner for food financing & will on-board Youlend for Poland. Since we will be distribution credit products, we will have to incur no costs or bear any financial responsibility. Relations between Bolt & Partner:

# Bolt role as distributor: Distribute the product to provider's on the Bolt Food App. Provider & Youlend will enter credit/partnership agreement.
# Bolt role as facilitator of repayment: Bolt will split the provider payout according to decided terms of repayment. Bolt will share % of provider payout with YouLend

The contract: 
Bolt will earn 20% commission on all credit products distributed through the Bolt ecosystem
On top of that, (Appendex 1) = Bolt will have option earn upto 7% more depending on performance of loans (If less defaults, more earnings){quote}

*Privacy Review results (7.10):*

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
Bolt and the provider will share data in a C2C arrangement. Current C2C clauses are vague and do not provide the same level of detail necessary to safeguard the transfer as default Bolt`s DSA.

Specific concerns:

* vague wording which makes the description of the transfer unclear, i.e. _“Partner (Bolt) acknowledges that it_ *_can choose_* _to provide Customer Data concerning Applicants”_
* the fact that Bolt will have access to customer Data (which may include Personal Data), including via the Partner Dashboard - not sure this is something that is required for our arrangement, and pursuant to the principle of data minimisation, we want to avoid unnecessary “data transfers”;
* _“To the extent that information is likely to be confidential, at a minimum the Applicant or Customer’s written consent is required”_ - this is unnecessary complication, I agree with your comment in the document.
* no details on how parties will cooperate in case of data breaches, inquiries from authorities, etc. Considering the sensitivity and the extent of the details shared by Bolt, our preference should be to include such procedures - which are outlined in our DSA.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
On a more general note, it is not clear to me why we would have to provide any personal data to the provider, considering that Bolt`s basic function is to distribute the offer from the provider to its merchants. Bolt`s should not be a part of the “decision making process” regarding the provider`s credit products.

*Bolt`s standard DSA template was shared & our concerns with the provider re/ excessive data transfer.*
{panel}

*UPD (21.11) - final position in YouLend`s DSA negotiations.*

Overall, the DSA was accepted as is with a few outstanding points:

* *Liability Cap* - we landed on aggregated liability cap for legal/privacy claims (not separate) of 100 000 EUR (instead of default 10 000 EUR). *Privacy position* - this is acceptable because: i) the amount of data subjects whose data will be transferred is very limited: dozens- max a few hundred merchants on Bolt Platform in Poland & Czechia; scope of personal data does not include special categories of data; YouLend will process the data as a data controller under its own responsibility, and not as a processor; *YouLend will indemnify Bolt against any losses incurred as a result of privacy law violations or breaches of the DSA by YouLend.*
* *Description of TOMs* - YouLend consistently refused to accept the online version of the [https://bolt.eu/en/security/supplier-requirements/|https://bolt.eu/en/security/supplier-requirements/|smart-link] . Instead, YouLend incorporated the online requirements that they could accept to Schedule 2 with TOMs. To be reviewed by Infosec - flagged to product.

*General note:* description of transfer and processing was updated to clarify the purpose of how YouLend will process the data as a separate data controller. The processing is not on behalf of Bolt, is done for separate purposes of YouLend, in accordance with Bolt's standard DPA. Bolt will not be responsible for these processing activities.

*UPD (28.11):*

* confirmed description in the DPA with product.
* product collaborates on confirming custom TOMs with Infosec.

*Privacy input finalised.* Asked reporter to keep privacy updated in the main ticket re/ signature process.

Hello [~accountid:60c88e6e8f2cc1006909fcf6],

We have investigated your request and have identified a couple of issues:

# The amount on the billed invoice is 847.80 EUR, which is correct:
## The breakdown of the invoice for September 2024 is:
### 836.80 EUR for Transport (that includes a proportion of the coupons, see next line)
### 11 EUR for ‘Kuponai (įvairioms paslaugoms)’, i.e. Coupon Usage
## According to the data from Balance Entries, the total amount is identical (847.80 EUR), however the breakdown is different:
### 824.80 EUR for Transport
### 23.00 EUR for Coupon Usage
## According to the numbers above, the Coupon Usage line on the invoice should be 23.00 EUR, so 12.00 EUR extra, and the Transport cost should be 12.00 EUR less.
## We do not know why this is, so we will escalate this to our Billing Engineers for them to investigate.
# The second issue, which is less important, but nonetheless worth mentioning, is that the CSV file does not include the Coupon Usage, so the total gross sum equals the amount in (b.i.) from above, i.e. 824.80 EUR.

Please inform your your client that due to the isolated nature of this incident, i.e. it has not affected any other users, we will not be able to issue a credit and reissue the invoice.

Feel free to apply an Apology Credit as necessary and please see the [attached file|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1t0jA1SawORcix5X5myI4oSM5aonqLEpPGO7laZn5rrc/edit?gid=315738788#gid=315738788] with the calculations for your reference.

h4. Blocking Matrix (Solving the safety event)

The consequential actions are defined by the Blocking Matrix (see table below).

The Blocking Matrix Quotient suggests the action that must be taken against the account of the *reported user* as per the *Risk Type* of the Event, number of *Occurrences* (User’s History), and *Event Confirmation* (whether we have evidence of the Event occurring or not). Once the information is selected in the Global Event Assessment Tool, an outcome will be proposed.

Blocking Matrix is always the first choice for the consequential action that should be applied. We should only use the option Deviant Action (i.e not implementing the action suggested by the Blocking Matrix) if the suggestion does not seem appropriate or when otherwise specified in the Standard Operating Procedures.

Some exceptions might apply. Read the Standard Operating Procedures carefully.

❗ It is essential to keep in mind that in some instances, *a Third Party might be at fault* - there should be no action taken against riders or drivers. (see Fault Determination table in the [Event confirmation and Fault Determination|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/50085?country=global&language=en#event-confirmation-and-fault-determination] section.



!https://images.bolt.eu//blockmatrix.png|width=1794,height=370,alt="matrix"!



*Consequential Actions*

* *Education* - Communicate to the user that such behaviour is not acceptable and educate them of best practices according to the event.
* *Warning* - Send a message warning the user that should this happen again, their account may be suspended. Communicate to them clearly that such behaviour is not acceptable.
* *1-Day Suspension, 3-Day Suspension, 7-Day Suspension* - Add the consequential suspension and set the length based on what the Blocking Matrix suggests. Communicate the decision to the user based on the Standard Operating Procedures.
* *Review Hard-Block* - Escalate the case to the Safety team with the High/Significant severity.

----

h4. Demerit Decay

Safety events have a Demerit Decay period, which indicates when a safety event has expired.

Search for any reports from the same Event Grouping from the reported user's Admin account and choose the number of previous reports together with the current report. Check the user’s comments, ratings, and previous events which have not yet decayed.

Consider the Demerit Decay period when doing so: older events should not be held against users when considering their previous offences and consequential actions.

* *Low and Moderate Risk Events* will decay after 3 months.
* *High Risk Events* will decay after 12 months.
* *Significant Risk Events* will not decay.

# When client requests change payment method, we need to first ask for driver confirmation and as this is asynchronous result, we need to wait for the driver response.
# There is not mechanism to pass over the 3ds or any other user related infomration in asynchronour request, so we need to return the data in active order response.

# As there will be change of preauthorisation order, information regarding the order will need to be asked after the driver has accepted the change, and as this is async process we will need to move the data flow from client services to booking services. 
# As the process is now asynchronous for the driver, we need to tell him if it was success or not, most likely new infomration message types need to be introduced. 
# We can reuse the confirmation storage for storing the payment method from and to as part of the payload and rely on it instead of the client provided (something might happen in between).
# We need to store the number of attemps we make, so that the driver confiramtion is only asked once.

* 2 identified approaches: 
1) one that relies on teams to build incremental denormed tables for reducing load on AB processor, 
2) one that uses dbt metric yamls for constructing queries from scratch but does not reduce load on AB processor
* Note: 2) is incompatible with 1) in how dbt metrics are defined in core tables that still require joins to become incremental denormed.
* An incremental denormed (called a Data Mart at Bolt) table looks like → multiple columns from different tables pre-joined, pre-aggregated (can be session/order?), and metrics pre-calculated incrementally with increments to enrollments table.
* dbt metrics looks like → a reference to a column in a [fact table|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DATA/pages/4591026531/Practical+guide+to+Data+Modelling+in+Bolt] (a type of semantic table), can have transformations defined ([example|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/rides/models/metrics/user/rides_demand_spend_rate.yml]). 
* semantic table looks like → not tables themselves but relations between core tables;

Question:

* is it possible to define a Data Mart from dbt metric yamls that provide the incremental denormed table starting point for XP metrics?
** this has advantage of incorporating dbt metric definition
** in majority of cases likely we won’t need additional metric transformations but we can always have additional metric yaml properties (perhaps also can be done via dbt) where needed

When a kafka broker is down, the expected behavior is all the producers gracefully transition to the healthy nodes, according with the new distribution of the topic’s partition.

The switchover is about two steps

* connect to healthy nodes to get the topics metadata
* connect to newly allocated brokers for establishing the new data plane.

In a successful switchover

* on server we should see a sudden increase to the create connection rate metric
* on client 
** when both of the above steps succeed, there should be no critical symptom (expect a slight increase in the send_duration)
** when one of the above steps fails, the NJSC producer should catch the error and automatically drop messages.

In the given AWS outage context

* we expect 2800-3000 instances simultaneously execute the switchover
* the client reports big delays to send_duration metric (up to 10 minutes) - signals of networking congestions, potential KafkaJS pool connection limits, KafkaJS locking
* the server reports a slight increase to the connections rate .

Of course, there are some authorities that may ask for information (e.g. Border Guards) but we are not legally obliged to respond but in case of prosecutors (dealing with serious crimes), there is usually no room for refusal.

h3. Summary of Kuwait key privacy requirements based on Al Tamimi & Company Kuwait advice 

[https://docs.google.com/document/d/12GUOr6zWN6YwuhNtR7-OgW4Z4EQ17wIq/edit#heading=h.30j0zll|https://docs.google.com/document/d/12GUOr6zWN6YwuhNtR7-OgW4Z4EQ17wIq/edit#heading=h.30j0zll|smart-link] 

# *Privacy regulations*:

_CITRA Resolution No. 26 of 2024_ and _Resolution No. 42 of 2021_ (collectively known as the Data Protection and Privacy Regulations or *DPPR*). DPPR apply to service providers licensed by CITRA, involved in the collection, processing, and storage of personal data, regardless of whether the processing takes place inside or outside Kuwait. *Bolt does not need a CITRA license for its operations* as it does not directly fall under CITRA’s licensing scope.

# *Data Breach Notification*:

Only licensed service providers must report data breaches to CITRA (within *24 hours* of discovery).

# *Direct Marketing*:

Licensed service providers are prohibited from sharing personal data with third parties for marketing purposes unless they have obtained prior consent from the user.

# *Data Localisation*:

If handling *Level 3* (private sensitive data) or *Level 4* (highly sensitive data), such data must be stored within Kuwait, particularly if using cloud services. This includes sensitive personal information like medical records, legal documents, and state security data. *Not applicable to Bolt.*

# *Cross-Border Data Transfers*:

There are no specific regulations for cross-border data transfers to the European Union other than obtaining customer consent. Including a statement in the *Privacy Notice* or *Terms & Conditions* is a common and accepted practice for obtaining consent.

# *Law Enforcement Data Access*:

Law enforcement authorities in Kuwait have the right to access personal data when necessary for criminal investigations, national security, or defence purposes.

# *Data Protection Officer (DPO)*:

There are no residency or citizenship requirements for the DPO, nor is there an official registration process with authorities.

* Workaround solution: Add hydration check useEffect hook, which also adds resize listeners. Hide form until hydration and it is determined if it is desktop or mobile. Conditionally render only one form

h3. 5.1 Automatically switch to the current location

*Problem:* When the user opens the app, we automatically save their previous location and suggest checking if their current location would be more relevant to their current session. It is hypothesized that some users may tend to close it immediately. This can affect the precision of the location and result in additional customer support costs when users request to update their location after placing an order.

*Solution:* When the app opens, automatically switch to the current location.

{noformat}SELECT invoice_id, uuid, source_type, created FROM (
select ie.id,ie.invoice_id,ie.uuid, ie.strategy, ie.source_type, ie.created, ie.state, ie.sum_with_vat, 
round(sum(ier.quantity * ier.unit_price * (1+ier.vat /100)),2) as sum_rows, 
ie.sum_with_vat - sum(ier.quantity * ier.unit_price * (1+ier.vat /100)) as diff from invoice_export ie
left join invoice_export_row ier on ier.invoice_id = ie.id
where ie.strategy  = 'PortugalFonoatechDelivery'
and ie.state in ('error','suspended')
group by ie.id, ie.invoice_id, ie.strategy, ie.uuid, ie.state, ie.sum_with_vat  
) summary
where summary.sum_rows is null or abs(summary.diff) > 0.02
order by created desc;
{noformat}

Hi all 👋  I’ve taken a look at this from the Privacy POV and have a few comments. These are summarised below. Happy to discuss if you have any questions.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*SUMMARY*

* I have made some assumptions based on the description of the arrangement, and have based my thoughts on these assumptions. As such, please let me know if any of these are incorrect.
* I recommend pushing for the inclusion of some additional light-touch data sharing provisions (drafted below) in the main agreement. We ordinarily push for these and it protects Bolt’s position.
* I recommend revising the wording in whichever consent form we go for (draft wording is below), as we need to make sure that each driver’s consent to the processing of their personal data in this context is _specific_ and _clear_. I would not recommend the current bespoke privacy notice in the longer-form consent form. I would also check with REP whether they are also collecting consent from the drivers to collect their images (whereas Bolt’s consent form relates to the use of the images of press).
* As there is a marketing element here, I am also looping in [~accountid:712020:b2a2738f-c1f1-447c-9b72-29851b5fed3e] for completeness - do you have anything you want to check on this?
{panel}

*Assumptions (please confirm accuracy)*

* REP London Limited will be taking photos / videos of 4 Bolt drivers, touching them up, and then sending them to Bolt UK Services Limited for Bolt’s use on social media / online / in press.
* Bolt will not be sending any driver personal data (e.g., their names, contact details etc.) to REP under this arrangement.

*Thoughts on Main Agreement (https://online.lightbluesoftware.com/client-portal/Raccoon-London/contracts/c95f2bcf0f76a2cc52040fd304551ffe.php)*

+*Context*+:
* Whenever Bolt enters into an arrangement with a third party that involves the sharing of personal data (e.g., REP sharing images / videos of drivers with Bolt), we ordinarily push for a data sharing agreement to be entered between the parties. This is so as to protect Bolt’s position should anything ‘go wrong’ with the data.
* If REP is just sharing limited data with Bolt under this arrangement, then the risk profile for Bolt is significantly lowered. Nevertheless, we need to ensure that Bolt’s bases are covered for case certain scenarios - for example, if REP are holding on to these images and suffer a data breach which causes the images to be used online in an unlawful manner, one of the Bolt drivers may want to take action against Bolt for this (being the entity most readily available to the driver). We need to ensure contractual protections are in place in case such scenarios occur.
+*Suggestion*+:
* Given the limited amount of data being shared, and the fact that REP is only sharing data with Bolt (and not vice-versa), IMO a full data sharing agreement / annex is not needed, particularly given the time sensitivity for this matter. Instead, we should propose the inclusion of a ‘data sharing clause’ in the main agreement.
* I propose asking for the inclusion of the following in the agreement. You will not this contains a pro-Bolt indemnity for data protection violations (which is a standard term we usually ask for) - this should not be subject to any liability cap.
_[X] Data sharing_
# _For the purposes of this Clause [X], the following definitions shall apply:_
## _“_*_Applicable Data Protection Law_*_” means the UK GDPR and any other applicable data protection laws;_
## _“_*_Relevant Personal Data_*_” means any Personal Data Processed pursuant to these Terms and Conditions, including but not limited to images of individuals;_
## _“_*_Personal Data_*_”, “_*_Personal Data Breach_*_” and “_*_Processing_*_” shall have the meaning set out in the UK GDPR; and_
## _“_*_UK GDPR_*_” means the General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as it forms part of the law in England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland by virtue of Section 3 of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018 and as amended by the Data Protection, Privacy and Electronic Communications (Amendments etc) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 and 2020 respectively, as well as any legislation in force in the United Kingdom from time to time that subsequently amends or replaces the UK GDPR._
# _Both parties acknowledge and agree, regarding the Processing of any Relevant Personal Data, to at all times ensure compliance with Applicable Data Protection Law. In particular, we hereby warrant, represent and undertake that all Relevant Personal Data shared by us with you, whether directly or indirectly, will be undertaken on the grounds of a valid lawful basis pursuant to Applicable Data Protection Law._ 
# _Both parties shall have in place appropriate technical and organisational security measures to protect any Relevant Personal Data._
# _Following the discovery of a Personal Data Breach affecting Relevant Personal Data, the compromised party shall notify the other party without undue delay (and in any event no later than forty-eight (48) hours after discovery of the Personal Data Breach), shall take appropriate steps to address the Personal Data Breach, and shall provide the other party with a full description of the Personal Data Breach and the steps taken to rectify the Personal Data Breach._
# _We shall, at all times during and after the term of these Terms & Conditions, defend, hold harmless and indemnify (at our own expense) you on demand against any claims, loss, damages, costs or expenses and other liabilities (including but not limited to legal fees) incurred by you arising out of or in connection with:_ 
## _any failure by us, our employees, subcontractors, or agents to comply with: (i) any of our obligations under this Clause [X]; and.or (ii) any Applicable Data Protection Law; and_
## _any Personal Data Breach concerning Relevant Personal Data suffered by us or caused by us whether directly or indirectly._


*Thoughts on the consent forms*

+*Context*+:
* On the assumption that REP is collecting the data and providing it to Bolt, REP must also ensure that they have a legal basis for processing the personal data connected to these images / videos (in the circumstances, consent also seems to be the most appropriate form). This is more REP’s concern than Bolt’s - however, it is worth knowing for completeness.
* Applicable data protection law requires that consent to data processing must be _specific_ (i.e., it should not be ‘bundled in’ with other consents) and _informed_ (i.e., the individual must be aware of exactly what they are consenting to) - otherwise, the consent is unlikely to be enforceable.
* I note that the longer of the two consent forms includes a draft privacy notice, that neither: (a) fully aligns with Bolt’s publicly-available privacy notice; nor (b) lists consent as a legal basis (which we are relying on here). I would therefore +*not*+ recommend using this draft.
+*Suggestion*+:
* We should ask REP what legal basis they are relying on in collecting and processing the driver’s data (i.e., their images / videos). If it is consent, are REP providing the drivers with a separate form?
* I propose either: (a) including a _separate_ form for consenting to personal data processing (i.e., separate to the consent for authorising use of image rights); or (b) including a separate section of the existing form in which the driver can provide an additional signature. In either case, the form needs to be clear that the user is consent to the processing of their personal data for specific / clearly defined purposes. It should read something like the following:
_I, the undersigned, consent to Bolt Operations OÜ, address Vana-Lõuna tn 15, Tallinn, company number 14532901, and its subsidiaries or partner companies of the Bolt Group (Bolt) processing my personal data which constitutes and is contained within any images and videos captured Bolt or by persons duly authorised by Bolt (including REP London Limited) for the purpose of marketing and advertising Bolt’s services in any media including but not limited to digital media formats such as banners, websites and social media platforms (including [_{color:#ff5630}_list social media platforms_{color}_])._
_I understand that the images and/or videos of me may be viewed globally, including in the countries that may not provide the same level of protection to the rights of individuals as the United Kingdom provides._ _I am aware that I may withdraw this consent at any time._
_[Signature / date / etc]_
_Further information on Bolt’s processing of your personal data can be found in the privacy notice available at:_ [_https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides_|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides]_._

Hi Dzmitry, 
Thank you for submitting your ticket!

The PIT-2 form is a document that allows your employer to apply tax relief directly to your monthly salary by reducing the amount of tax deducted from your paycheck. It’s linked to the standard tax-free allowance in Poland, which is applied throughout the year.

When you sign the PIT-2 form, your employer can reduce the amount of personal income tax (PIT) deducted from your salary each month, which slightly increases your net pay. If you don’t sign it, you will still receive the tax relief, but it will be applied after you file your annual tax return, meaning you could get a larger tax refund instead of seeing it spread out over the year in your monthly salary.

Signing it is optional, so it’s up to you whether you prefer the relief to be reflected in your monthly paycheck or if you would rather receive the total amount when you file your taxes. 

Let me know if you need further clarification!

Cheers,
Olena

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

SQL used:
The polygons in the city table are not closed and Presto does not like that. I had to close them in SQL before using them.

{noformat}with cities as (select c.id, c.name, c.polygon from glue.ng_public.admin_system_city c
	where ST_IsClosed(ST_GeometryFromText(CONCAT('LINESTRING(', c.polygon , ')'))) = true
	and c.polygon is not null
	and c.polygon != ''
	and c.market_type_rentals != 'inactive'
	union 
	select c.id, c.name , CONCAT(c.polygon, ',', REPLACE(REPLACE(ST_AsText(ST_StartPoint(ST_GeometryFromText(CONCAT('LINESTRING(', c.polygon , ')')))), 'POINT (', ''), ')', '')) as polygon from glue.ng_public.admin_system_city c
	where ST_IsClosed(ST_GeometryFromText(CONCAT('LINESTRING(', c.polygon , ')'))) = false
	and c.polygon is not null
	and c.polygon != ''
	and c.market_type_rentals != 'inactive'
)	            
select c.id as city_id, c.name, pa.id as area_id from glue.ng_public.smart_pickups_area pa
join cities c on pa.city_id = c.id 
and pa.snap_polygon is not null
and pa.snap_polygon != ''
and pa.is_deleted = false
and pa.state != 'disabled'
and ST_Contains(ST_GeometryFromText(concat('POLYGON((',c.polygon, '))')),
	            ST_GeometryFromText(concat('POLYGON((',pa.snap_polygon , '))'))) = false{noformat}

Hey!

In my opinion, the driver is in the right at the moment.

There is no legal requirement to have a valid ID-card - rather, it is a _nice to have_ document.

The rider is granted the right to render services if they have a valid driver’s license - checking that document might be apt. 

The law states that an Estonian resident must have a personal identification document. And a driver’s license could be considered as one. 

In addition, to become the renderer of services in ride-hailing, you have to present your driver’s license. But there is no direct requirement of having an ID-card. If the driver’s license expires - yes, that is understandable as you cannot operate a vehicle without a valid license. 

In my opinion, we are restricting the right to use the platform without any legal grounds and the driver should be granted access to the platform. 

Proposal to solve the situation: grant access to the driver and state something vague a’la “_We considered your opinions and your access right has been restored until we discuss this requirement internally. Thank you for bringing this up._”

If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error.

* Total: 278.24 + 50.10 = 328.34 EUR
* Service Fee (pre-VAT) = 328.34 * 10% = 32.83 EUR
* Service Fee (with VAT) = 32.83 + 19%  = 39.07 EUR

The Service Fee is 0.01 EUR too much, due to a known rounding issue, that the Billing Engineers are currently working on.

Ultimately our polices are generally supportive of Bolt’s policies as we typically seek to align with good global practices and behave in a socially responsible and ethical manner, but we do so in compliance with Etisalat’s requirement and not because we are committing contractually with any particular customer or any other third party’s policy.

_5.2 Etisalat acknowledges that it has received and read Partner’s Supplier Code of Conduct and confirms that its Own Code of Conduct takes social responsibility and ethical issues seriously and is aligned with Partner’s Supplier Code of Conduct. Long time ago we added the logic which after battery id is changed reopened the task but keep charger who started the task as the resolver. Otherwise battery swap would stuck until 8h autoresolve timeout passes and no one else could finish it because task is still in_progress.
But it brings us an issue like in the report. When task gets reopened it is no longer need to be compliant with all close criteria (one of which is the 60% battery level threshold). Hello Monika! 

Thanks for flagging. 

* _If the agent works on both tiers, should the additional non-safety issues simply be added as issue tags without escalations while the tier and severity remain the same (safety, low/high)?_
** If the agent is trained and can handle both Safety and Non-Safety, then they should add all the needed tags (safety and non-safety). The ticket does not need to be de-escalated anywhere, Tier stays in Safety as well as severity. 
* _If the agent works only on safety cases, and he needs to de-escalate the case to tier1, should the ticket eventually be closed with safety tier or tier1?_
** If a Safety agent is not trained to handle the non-safety part of the ticket, they can de-escalate to Tier 1 and it will be closed in Tier 1. This applies reverse as well. If a ticket starts as non-safety and becomes safety, we move to Safety Tier and it will remain there. 
* _Also, if it needs to be closed with tier1, should the severity be none or any risk type due to previously solved safety case?_
** If there is a safety case that needs to be de-escalated to Tier 1 and solved there (if there is a non-safety case that Safety agent cannot solve), the Tier changes, but the *severity MUST remain.* 
* _In case that the ticket is closed with tier1, will relevant teams be able to extract the necessary data for safety analysis later (keeping in mind that safety issues are the most important ones)?_
** Yes, the is why it is vital that the severity remains on safety tickets even if the Tier has to change. 
* _If the case needs to be closed by tier1 agent who is not working on safety cases, how can he be sure that the safety issue has been completely and correctly solved/closed (also keeping in mind that the closing agent should check that all the data is correct before solving it)?_
** When a safety case needs to be de-escalated to Tier 1 (in cases where safety agent cannot resolve the non-safety issue), it is up to the Safety agent to ensure that the safety part is completed accordingly before de-escalating to Tier 1. 



Hope this helps!

Hello [~accountid:6215e9d79cd4a70071de651c],

From what I understand, there is a misunderstanding that a rebate can be applied for in a given month and applied against the costs of that same month, but that is not how rebates work.

Rebates are issued the month after being applied for, and can be used against the next month’s invoice, before the rebate expires at the end of the month, as per the information on this [page|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/2952889522/How+rebate+works].

So, the *rebate applied for in July*, was *available to be used in August* and *expired at the end of August.*

In this case, you have applied for a 20% rebate for the amount for the invoice for the month of July 2024 (excluding the Service Fee):

* *Amount used to calculate rebate:* 3,250.18 - 178.24 = *3071.94 EUR*
* *Rebate amount:* 3071.94 x 20% = *614.39 EUR*

Looking in [Balance Entries|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/business-invoicing/businessCompanies/edit/328633?tab=balance_entries&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A50%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D] I can see this amount was created as a rebate on 2014-08-02:

!image-20241008-223008.png|width=100%,alt="image-20241008-223008.png"!

A [credit note|https://doclink.live.boltsvc.net/invoice/pdf?i=PT4524-813&k=a1caa91f6ae58cafc264ac81ffdc52b6] for 320.50 EUR was created from the rebate to pay for the August invoice, as you can see in the [Rebates|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/business-invoicing/businessCompanies/edit/328633?tab=rebates&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A50%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D] tab:

!image-20241008-225325.png|width=100%,alt="image-20241008-225325.png"!

Deducting the above leaves:

* *Remaining rebate amount:* 614.39 - 320.50 = *293.89 EUR*, as shown below:

!image-20241008-225115.png|width=100%,alt="image-20241008-225115.png"!

As you can see above, the 293.89 EUR amount that remained is marked as Unused Rebate, as the amount spent in August was not enough to use the rebate in full.

I aligned with your advice. Bolt Thailand should avoid requiring users to upload the back of their ID cards (containing lazer number used mainly by only the government or local bank institutions) due to the risks it poses to user privacy and security. 
Additionally, under Thailand’s Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), companies are obligated to protect personal information, and limiting the collection of sensitive data helps ensure compliance and reduces legal risks.

Hi [~accountid:712020:f63df97f-cad1-4718-9bb1-80038488d7e2] , with regard to the problem described in the ticket, I know that we have a provision in the T&Cs re. failure to return the tablet (5.4.) ((_…) If the Partner fails to return the rented devices and any other equipment, Bolt may impose a contractual penalty in the amount equivalent to the value of the device or keep the deposit if a deposit was applied. (…)),_ however, *such provision is likely to be deemed unenforceable in Poland, therefore Bolt may not be able to demand payment of the penalty.* 
In Poland, there is a legal requirement of indicating the amount of a contractual penalty:

* in the specific amount (e.g. PLN 1000) or 
* (at least) by giving the description that leaves no doubt as to the amount of the penalty (e.g. cost of the Apple iPad Pro 2 at [x.com|http://x.com] as of the date of when the tablet should be returned to Bolt). 

In my opinion, our T&Cs do not meet the above requirement, therefore I suggest adding a draft clause to the agreement in which the amount of contractual penalty will be directly indicated, e.g. 

“_In case the rented device is not returned to Bolt within […] days from the date on which the agreement was terminated, the Partner will pay a contractual penalty in the amount of PLN […] per unreturned device. The Partner acknowledges that within the period specified in the preceding sentence, the device shall be directly delivered to the Company by mail or courier, whereby the day of delivery shall also be considered the day on which the first delivery attempt was made. Delivery of the device after the lapse of the 30-day period shall not release the Partner from the obligation to pay the contractual penalty referred to in this clause._”.

FYI - the penalty does not have to be equivalent of the value of the device. It cannot be grossly excessive but we are free to demand e.g. PLN 2000 even if the value of the device is PLN 100.

In my opinion, we are free to introduce waiting fee as described in the ticket, provided that the amount will not exceed maximum amounts indicated in applicable resolutions regarding maximum prices for taxi services.

* *Clause 4.7 of the T&Cs directly indicates possibility to apply the waiting fee* “_Gdy kierowca przyjedzie na miejsce i wyśle powiadomienie o swoim przybyciu, aplikacja Bolt może rozpocząć naliczanie opłaty za oczekiwanie według stawek określonych w aplikacji Bolt_.”
* Additionally, clause 1.3. mentions that the total fee may include additional fees “_(…) Opłaty mogą uwzględniać inne należne opłaty, opłaty drogowe lub opłaty dodatkowe, w tym opłaty rezerwacyjne, opłaty miejskie, opłaty lotniskowe lub opłaty za przetwarzanie płatności podzielonych. (…)_”
* *The amount of waiting fee should not exceed maximum amounts indicated in applicable resolutions regarding maximum prices for taxi services*, e.g. in Warsaw it is PLN 50 per hour which would require from us setting a maximum waiting fee as PLN 0,83 per minute.
* *The maximum amount should be applicable to all categories*, meaning that the above amount per minute would apply both to economy and premium category.
* I do not believe that we should do anything before introducing the waiting fee because, as mentioned, T&Cs allow us to apply this fee. Of course, the team should focus on providing relevant information about the waiting fee in the app but this can be made based on other countries where the fee has been already in force, [e.g. Spain|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1x0Bmufaqrm8-ABn4nzJmDLDmXJ3DkR-AZo8bcLzNOcg/edit?gid=1625058149#gid=1625058149].

Hey Monika! 

Thanks for flagging to us.

After doing some thinking on this, we came to the following conclusions: 

* We will add a note in the tool guidelines in KB that we should always select the higher risk type in the tool if there is more than 1 event.
* If there are two event categories of the same risk type, it does not matter what is selected in the tool. However, if the driver has a precedent for one of the event categories, select this one in the tool. We will add some clarification as well.



However, it is important to note that we should always be actioning all the event categories that are identified in the case. For example, if we have a Groping case and the rider identified that the driver was not the same, we still need to address all allegations with the driver (meaning the groping allegation and not being the same). If the driver denies groping, but has a precedent for not being the same, while it will not be selected in the tool, we should still take action based on the blocking matrix.

** On 10 June 2024, the email address on Account 2 was changed to [raimondss.lukauskas@splius.lt|mailto:raimondss.lukauskas@splius.lt] (“*Email Address 2*”), and the phone number was changed from the Old Phone Number to +37066795522 (the “*New Phone Number*”).

- delete all custom favorite suggestions since we do not want to show them in the quick suggestions

As always, when we receive a request, we follow these steps from privacy POV:

* 1️⃣ *_See if the information they requested is personal data._* 
** In this case, fleet contact details can be provided.
** However, they had another request: “Also for each of the above to inform us with the *date of start of work and to send us the portion (I assume they mean tax information) of each with the total production (they mean earnings) and the amount collected from the date of start of work.*” 
*** As far as I understand, this information relates to specific couriers and not fleets. If my understanding is correct, then the data is personal data and we need to follow the further steps I am outlining above.
* 2️⃣ *_See if they have provided us with a reference to a law that obligates us to disclose the personal data._* This is a step required by the GDPR, namely, we need to have a *legal obligation* or another alternative legal basis that facilitates this data sharing.
** Again, this step only applies to courier and not fleet data. So, I would suggest asking them to provide a reference to a law that gives them the right to request data / gives us an obligation to disclose the data. As per our process, we use the following template (Feel free to adjust the wording as you see fit):


{quote}Hi ${user_firstname},

we acknowledge your request *EDIT: Specify an ongoing document or file number*, dated *EDIT: Specify the date request received.*

Firstly, we wanted to assure you that ${brand} understands the seriousness of this request and we look to assist law enforcement whenever we are able to.

At ${brand}, we take the privacy and security of our customers, employees, and independent contractors very seriously. We only engage in data sharing with third parties where we are satisfied that the requirements of our third party data sharing policy have been met. This means that the request for data is lawful, necessary, proportionate, and limited to the specific purpose outlined in the request.

After carefully reviewing your request, we have determined that you have not provided us with a reference to the specific law or regulation that obliges ${brand} to disclose the data requested. In this instance, ${brand} will be unable to meet its legal requirements for establishing a legal basis for data disclosure.

To allow us to validate your request, we kindly advise you to provide a reference to the specific law or regulation which allows ${brand} to release this data. Providing the necessary details will enable us to properly process your request in accordance with applicable privacy laws and regulations.{quote}

* 3️⃣ *_If the legal basis is valid, and the request is proportionate, we can disclose the data._*

I did another test today. I turned the butterfly valve to absolute maximum open position (brake was already stuck at this point) and then checked how much brake pad material we can use up by setting up the caliper at 80mm (drum ID) and comparing to the brake pads. 

If you look at the bottom picture you can see that when the brake is expanded all the way like this, we can only use up slightly less than 50% of the pad material. 

In my opinion this means that any kind of modification to the brake arm will not fix our problem. We might get slightly more life out of the pads, but we will not be able to utilize the pads until the end of the lifetime. And expanding the brake this far can produce a possibly very *hazardous situation*, as at some point the butterfly will jam and pads will not return any more, meaning the wheel will lock up even if the brake lever on the bars is released.

*BACKGROUND*

* Original request on [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-35677|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-35677|smart-link] (assigned to Topazia).
* Request from German lawyer (Attorney Oliver Mölleken, ref 52213598-DE1124-620) on behalf of Mr Al-Taie (Bolt driver). Passenger (Mrs Bloch) allegedly smoked in the car, causing burn damage. “_In order to enforce the legal claims, we are dependent on Mrs Bloch's address details being sent to us_”.
** Attached power of attorney - Provides unrestricted authorisation to conduct proceedings (did not explicitly mention authorised to conduct DSARs).
** This is not a DSAR, as it is requesting the data of a third-party (i.e., the rider). As such, it is more akin to a LER.
* On 18 June 2024, Topazia instructed the following to be sent: ”_We note that you have not yet provided us with a legal basis_ _for your request for personal data in accordance with Article 6 GDPR. In order for us to review your request, we require a reference to the specific law or regulation that authorises you to request this data. Without this, Bolt will be unable to meet the requirements of Article 6 GDPR and therefore be unable to assist you. Providing a legal basis will expedite your request, and prevent further delays in assisting you”._
* On 17 July, the lawyer responded with “_we are unable to understand it. You do not explain on whose behalf you are acting and what your relationship is to the claims submitted to the other party's motor vehicle liability insurance._
_We request clarification so that we can provide you with appropriate information_”.
* On 7 August, Topazia instructed CS to reject the request on the grounds of no legal basis.
* On 27 September, the lawyer responded with “_We would like to point out that we are therefore obliged to initiate criminal proceedings against your customer for damage to property… your customer will be subject to criminal proceedings. We therefore assume that your customer herself is interested in you forwarding the data accordingly. We ask you to contact your customer and discuss this with her. We will give you another opportunity to send the data within 7 days, otherwise we will report the matter to the police and initiate criminal proceedings against your client_.”
* The present ticket was created on 7 October.

*THOUGHTS*

* We do not typically provide data to third parties that are not law enforcement agencies / pubic authorities, and we do not have a formalised process in place that covers this kind of request.
* However, we have provided the address of a Bolt user to lawyers in the past (see e.g., [+LSS-37805+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-37805]). We have done so on the basis of Bolt having a strong legitimate interest in doing so in light of the context (i.e., if we are aware of bad practice from the user and that a law firm wants to bring legal proceedings against them).
* Ultimately, the data being requested here is limited (it is just the rider’s address, which makes sense for the purpose of serving formal proceedings on them). I have also googled the lawyer ([here|https://anwalt-moelleken.de/]) and they do exist.
* It is unclear how else the lawyer would get hold of correspondence details of the rider in order to serve legal proceedings. As such, we do not want to be causing any frustration of seeking legal justice here.
* This matter has already had some back-and-forth and is escalating. It is not as if we are by default giving away the address - we are doing so given the current state of the matter as-is.

*PROPOSED NEXT STEPS*

* Double-check with CS: (1) what is the rider’s address; and (2) have we received any complaints about the trip in CS tickets that legitimise the allegations being made here?

* *_Address_*_: [X]_
_We trust that the information will be only used in connection with initiating legal proceedings against the passenger, and only held and used as long as it is required for that purpose._

Hi Thomas,

Please see below my answers, thank you:

_So Art.23 lit. d-e from GEO 49/2019 effectively requires drivers to have: (1) a criminal record certificate showing that they have not committed certain crimes; and (2) a medical / psychological certificate showing they are fit to drive. To be clear on this - do we have both of these documents on record for this driver? -_ *Bolt Operations - Ops is requesting only the criminal record, to double check that the driver is fit for providing services on our platform. Ops is not requesting the medical certificate, most likely for GDPR reasons. However, according to the law, these two documents (criminal and medical) have to be submitted by the driver/transport operator to the Romanian Road Authority - ARR. ARR is then checking these documents and issues the authorisation for providing transport services. With this authorisation, the drivers/transport operator is allowed by Bolt to register on the platform.* 

_If the ANPC have requested both the criminal record certificate and the medical certificate, and if we are required to provide them, why have we decided to only provide one and not the other?_ - *this is the catch. According to the law, there is no obligation for Bolt to request these two certificates (criminal and medical), these should be submitted to ARR by the driver/transport operator. But, Ops decided to also request the criminal record for business and safety reasons. If ARR decides, based on the criminal record, that the driver is allowed to hold a transport authorisation, maybe Bolt, based on the criminal record, may conclude that the driver’s history is not fit for what we want to offer to our customers.* 

_Have we responded to any similar ANPC requests of this nature in the past?_ - *I don’t recall having similar requests from them.* 

Sorina

As said below, in most cases, the creation or retention of copies of ID documents (such as driver's licenses or ID cards) is unlawful. Employers may only request to view these documents in specific and justified circumstances, such as verifying a driver's eligibility to operate a vehicle. However, this verification process does not typically permit the making or storing of copies of the documents.

As we are not acting as employers in this instance, it is even more challenging to justify the processing of such copies. I can confirm that processing copies of identification documents is only permitted in a very limited number of situations, subject to legal restrictions.

I have gone through the Labour Code, ID Documents Act provisions and could not find any exemption that we would be able to utilise in this case, unfortunately.

For cases where refund was issued but can’t be seen on the user’s card or Bolt balance.

* Check where the refund was sent to and if it was successful on the [transaction history page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22target_account_id%22%3A%2265766018%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] 
** If Bolt balance refund is successful, there is a green button after the refund “🟢 success”
** If refund to card, 💳 success
* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.
** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments
* Only successful card payments can be refunded to card.

Dear Monir,

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 10 September 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties (including the rights of passengers). Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled, in particular your trip history on 10 October 2023.

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our privacy notice available at [https://bolt.eu/es-es/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/es-es/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

** We take your privacy seriously. As a part of this commitment, we would like to clarify our practices of collecting your location information.

In terms of usability will be sub-optimal as the user might have to run the pipeline several times to fix all the issues.

The new approach fully covers the security aspects (user won’t be able to generate incidents), but trades usability for cost.

For cases where refund was issued but can’t be seen on the user’s card or Bolt balance.

* Check where the refund was sent to and if it was successful on the [transaction history page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22target_account_id%22%3A%2265766018%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] 
** If Bolt balance refund is successful, there is a green button after the refund “🟢 success”
** If refund to card, 💳 success
* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.
** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments
* Only successful card payments can be refunded to card.

Hi Team,

Please be informed that the product legal team from Estonia considers that the stragegy of rejecting couriers as explained is a big risk for reclassification. In their opinian we shouldn’t be rejecting couriers. When couriers sign up on the platform this has to be seen as a “registration“ and not an “acceptance by Bolt“. If a courier registers in the platform - by accepting the T&Cs - they become a business user and Bolt cannot reject the courier without increasing reclass risk. If Bolt claims to be an “intermediary“ platform, Bolt cannot be accepting/rejecting couriers - exception couriers who have been terminated from the platform earlier for e.g. fraud or safety reasons.

We also believe that this situation creates risks that should be avoided, since it is not clear if the T&Cs allows to reject couriers without a legitimate reason.

In this case and taking all this into account +we suggest making an agreement between lawyers and give access to this courier (finalising the onboarding), pay the court fee and drop out the indemnity amount (10K)+. [~accountid:5fb258e1f2df6c00762dac23] do you agree on this strategy?

If we are going to go ahead with the agreement, it should be concluded before the deadline to present the defence - before 28 October.

Thank you!

Hi [~accountid:60f2a71843c956007065f2ad] - apologies, I am still a bit confused. Why are we talking about Bolt “requesting” documents when we are to be the ones _providing_ them to the ANPC?

If helpful, I summarise below Privacy’s view on responding to requests of this nature - in short, we can respond to the request with the requested info if the request is *valid*, with a *legitimate basis*, and *proportionate*.

* *Valid*: We have been corresponding with ANPC on this for a while, so it looks like we have no issues in terms of verifying the  requestor. We therefore how no issues on this.
* *Legitimate basis*: Below, we have been discussing GEO 49/2019, which I understand “_obliges us to cooperate with Consumer Protection Authority_” - however: (a) does the same law +_specifically require Bolt to provide the documents when it receives a request from ANPC_+; or (b) is the obligation to cooperate instead a general one?
** If it is (a), and the ANPC has requested the criminal certificate and the medical certificate, then we should provide these.
* If it is (b), then we would look at *proportionality* - this is primarily where Privacy input kicks in. To do so, I would need to see the two documents and then I would be able to provide my views. 
** If these documents contain too much sensitive personal data, then we could take the approach of flagging that: (1) the driver is certified for ride-hailing by the ARR; and (2) the requested documents are verified by the ARR before it issues authorisations. We could then refrain from provide the documents on that basis (which I believe aligns with what you are saying below).
** While I appreciate the logic in the suggestion to provide the Professional ride-hailing driving certificate (front and back), Car registration certificate, “Compliant copy” and ARR Sticker, I would be hesitant to provide these to the ANPC unless they are _specifically_ requesting them.

Does that all make sense? Apologies if I am missing something here! 🙂

h3. *Summary of the Data Processing Addendum (DPA)*

*Conclusion:*

The DPA appears robust, covering both international transfers and GDPR compliance.

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*However, the following problems were identified:*

# Bolt is put in the position of a data processor, needs to comply with very strict, and likely, unrealistic, requirements under Art. 28 GDPR - detailed below - section 4.
# From the description, it is not clear why Bolt will have to process data both as a controller and a processor.
# The description of the transfer is generally unclear. Purposes are essentially missing, and are described as “AWX Controller Purposes” or “Customer” (Bolt) purposes.
{panel}

Recommended course of action:

# request to clarify the applicability of “processor clauses” to Bolt; request to remove them.
# request to clarify the data transfer arrangement, to ensure a detailed description of the transfer.
# request to clarify if [Bolt`s Infosec Code of Practice|https://bolt.eu/en/security/supplier-requirements/#:~:text=You%20must%20implement%20information%20security,privacy%20controls%20have%20been%20implemented.] can be applied - at least where it acts as a data controller.

Details of the summary:

*1. Data Transfer Arrangement:*

Two way transfer:
*AWX to Bolt*: *C2C transfer - AWX* to *Bolt*: Data like Account Data transferred to Bolt for its own Controller Purposes.
*Bolt to AWX*: transfers are both *C2C* and *P2C.*
* *C2C Transfers*:
** Purposes: unspecified. Bolt transfers Onboarding Data and Account Data (e.g., transaction details, account information) to AWX for AWX’s own independent purposes.
* *P2C Transfers*:
** Purposes: Onboarding Data: to enable KYC and onboarding in respect of the Embedded Finance Solution as required by Airwallex and to facilitate Airwallex’s compliance with its obligations under Applicable Law; Support Data: to provide customer support in respect of the Embedded Finance Solution.

*2. Cross-Border Data Transfers:*

* No international transfers occur as both AWX (Netherlands) and Bolt (Estonia) are EU entities. 
* However, the DPA covers international transfers and satisfies GDPR and UK GDPR's requirements for such transfers. 
* EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and the UK Information Commissioner’s International Data Transfer Addendum (IDTA) are attached and include correct information.
* *Dutch law and supervisory authority applies where AWX is the data exporter.*
* *Estonian law and supervisory authority can apply where Bolt is the data exporter.*

*3. C2C Compliance Clauses - applicable to AWX*

While Article 28 GDPR does not apply directly to AWX (since it acts as the Data Controller in all cases), the DPA does outline similar safeguards and procedures to ensure AWX's compliance when processing personal data.
On high level, these include:
* *General authorisation of engagement of “Approved Transferees”* - similar to sub-processor authorisation under Art. 28. List of “*Transferees” is available.*
* *Robust AWX security measures* (*Annex 2*).
* *Data breach notification* (24 hours) and *data retention* limitations.
* *Audit rights* for *Bolt* to verify *AWX's compliance* - does not include actual audits / on-site audits, but simply undertaking to share all information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance.


*4. Where Bolt acts as a data processor:*

No gaps in relation to Article 28 GDPR requirements based on the DPA's content - requirements are quite strict:
# *Data Breach Notification:*
* Notification of any data breach affecting AWX personal data within 24 hours (general data) or 4 hours (Singapore data).
* Relevant Clause: Section 5.12
# *Audits and Inspections*
* *On-site audits* are permitted with *3 days' notice*;
* Audits can occur up to *once per year*, unless triggered by a *security incident* or a request by a regulator.
* Auditors can inspect facilities, systems, and processes used to process *AWX’s* data.
* Relevant Clause: Section 5.9
# *Data Subject Rights Procedure*
* Notification: If Customer must notify AWX immediately, and no later than *2 business days* after receiving the request.
* Relevant Clause: Section 5.14
# *Subprocessors:*
* General authorisation with 20 days notice;
* Bolt must keep a list of sub-processors and update it.
* Relevant Clause: Section 5.15
Other problematic requirements: Bolt must comply with AWX security measures, return or delete data at the end of the contract; and comply with other restrictions under Art. 28.
*Bolt will likely push back as accepting the status of a data processor is problematic for our compliance.*


*5. C2C Compliance Clauses - applicable to AWX and Bolt*

Here is what I advised in the business-tech-support Slack channel a while ago. Would it be doable?

*Background and legal framework*

* UNHCR are entitled to receive invoices with 0% VAT if they have given the service providers a specific certificate for tax exemption: [https://www.vm.ee/sites/default/files/documents/2024-01/VAT%20excise%20duty%20exemption%20certificate.pdf|https://www.vm.ee/sites/default/files/documents/2024-01/VAT%20excise%20duty%20exemption%20certificate.pdf]
* Since they are currently on intermediary model then by the book UNHCR should give this certificate to all the individual drivers as they are seen as the service providers in this context

* A switch to reseller model would help as then the service provider to UNHCR (at least from a tax perspective) would be Bolt and not the individual drivers

*What needs to be done in order to be compliant and help the client (if doable from operational and technical perspective)*

* Ask for the certificate if we don't have it yet
* Switch UNHCR to reseller model so the certificate can be for Bolt Ops
* Credit the invoices with VAT
* Issue new invoices for the past and future periods without VAT and a disclaimer - "The supply is exempt from VAT based on art 42 par 3 of the Belgian VAT code"

Hello Iiris,

Thank you for your response. Firstly, I realize that my initial reply may have been brief and unclear, so I’d like to provide more context.

The decision that 'Rider consuming illegal drugs would be considered as Rider Transporting Illegal Drugs' was not made arbitrarily or without Risk Review. In fact, this is explicitly stated in the Risk Review [document|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1rJ_jy-ohyRJLS-ZzlJgNQGugNjo5HAdfBj5yZ3QwH28/edit?gid=610408630#gid=610408630], which specifies that drug consumption by riders is classified as transporting illegal drugs. Furthermore, the document also clarifies that drug consumption by drivers is classified as Driver Intoxication. This document was shared with the teams prior to the review, allowing time for any questions or concerns to be raised.

To explain why rider drug consumption is treated differently from driver drug consumption: as a company, we place significant importance on our reputation and cannot tolerate any form of drug use by drivers on our platform, as it directly impacts us. However, while we cannot control the behavior of riders, we must still take action against bad actors.

Upon reviewing your ticket again, I’d like to address any misunderstanding. Your comment that “*It is not logical to take Rider owning drugs, but not take them consuming them*” is specified in our process - where 'Rider consuming illegal drugs is treated as Rider Transporting Illegal Drugs.'

Additionally, in reference to your point about drug ownership not being a safety concern, I would note that it’s challenging to determine drug possession unless it is visibly exposed. However, drug *consumption* puts the driver in a potentially risky situation where it is impossible to predict how the rider will behave. 

Please let me know what specific areas require further clarification. As you’ve noted, the Risk team cannot make sudden changes mid-process without undergoing a formal Risk Review. However, we are always open for feedback, and if the change you're suggesting is directed more to case examples, feel free to provide your suggestions. We will assess whether the examples can be updated accordingly. As you’re aware, safety processes are not set in stone and can be adjusted when it makes sense to do so.

Cheers,

Galina

# *Argument against Court’s decision to not entertain Bolt’s defense that it acted with reasonable care*. 

* Surely there is a defense here that we were entitled to reasonably assume that the person registering the profile, with all relevant documents, was indeed the data subject in the documents?
* The Court references that it denied Bolt’s defense on the following basis:

_This court respectfully declines this invitation._ *_The court's decision stems from Sections 28 of Act 843_*_, which impose an obligation on D2 to implement measures that ensure the integrity of the personal data it collects and processes._

* The Court has erred in its application of Section 28 to the act of _‘collecting_’ the personal data. Section 28, read plainly, is specifically intended to prevent: “(a) loss of, damage to, or unauthorised destruction; and (b) unlawful access to or unauthorised processing of personal data”, by requiring a Data Controller to “_take the necessary steps to secure the integrity of personal data in the possession or control_.” *Bolt suffered none of these circumstances*.

# The Court makes reference to a “compromise” of a data processor’s database and the need for an audit. *The Court errs when it equates a failure to perform additional verification, with a breach of one’s systems and the need for a forensic audit*. In doing so, it has taken Bolt’s breach of its duty of care out of context and extended it to something that did not occur — a data breach:

* The Court’s order for the Data Protection Commission to audit Bolt’s system is preceded by an opinion from the Court that in the event of a compromise of a database “_it is imperative to take action. First, an appropriate audit of the IT system and database should occur. This audit serves two essential purposes; sanitizing the database and ensuring public safety. By conducting a forensic audit, any fraudulently or falsely registered profiles can be identified and removed_”. 
* The Court uses this reasoning to justify its Order for the DPC to conduct a forensic audit of Bolt and for the record, we should be arguing against it on the basis that it is irrelevant.

Current takeaways:

# Not all networks support eDRX (in Tallinn only Telia does)
# Even if network supports eDRX, it’s parameters depend on network, i.e. the modem can request certain eDRX and paging intervals but the actual values would be determined by an operator. Telia always suggest to use default ones.
# eDRX itself doesn’t give any noticeable power gains by itself. This is rather an indication to the modem that it can enter a sleep power mode if it has such a capability.
# With EG915u and USB as a host interface the sleep mode is only possible if USB host suspends modem into low-power mode or if it takes VBUS power down. 
# ESP32-S3 host controller does support suspend function though it doesn’t seem like it is supported in the public API (under investigation currently, it maybe only possible through esp-idf code modification).
# To enable low power mode in future designs with Quectel modems we either have to switch to UART interface or use an USB host which supports suspend/resume functionality.

The cited law (_§ 29 (1) (a) of Act No. 56/2012 Coll. on Road Transport_) mentions the obligations of taxi operators, focusing on making sure taxi services are provided by drivers in an employment relationship with the operator.

However, from privacy POV, it does not explicitly obligate us to *disclose personal data* to an authority. The general duties mentioned in the law focus more on operational aspects (e.g., employment relationships) rather than data sharing obligations.

So, from a privacy perspective, we can do the following:

* let them know that we need a reference to a law that gives them the right to receive this data → we still haven’t received that
* [~accountid:62b2cf3c0c77011bdfdcdbcd] if you believe that non-disclosure in this case poses us significant risks - we can rely on an alternative legal basis (legitimate interest to disclose data to facilitate their investigation under GDPR). But I’d use this one as a last resort in case the investigation is serious.

When it comes to reclassification, we have *accepted a minimum level of risk* and, when managing reclassification risk, it is important first of all *that the existing market risk does not increase.*

* This means that a *feature or logic can be exchanged for something else in order to maintain* or reduce the *risk level* in a market. This logic increases the existing market risk around *-23 % and is a high risk logic.* We could do this e.g. if we ask local markets to stop incentivising drivers based on OH and AR and use this logics instead as this is in the same risk category. Hey [~accountid:712020:7f47c2af-14e1-4206-a795-ac87cb906276],
as discussed earlier this week here’s our advise and assessment on the DQO. Please read it carefully. Based on your market situation there are steps to follow.

* Here you find our assessment on DQO: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Crtd8oaVVwcgwRixEP8YTTW1A-i3zFrZ_T9D73mhlbs/edit?tab=t.0|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Crtd8oaVVwcgwRixEP8YTTW1A-i3zFrZ_T9D73mhlbs/edit?tab=t.0|smart-link]
* General recommendation:
** *DQO is a high risk feature*
** If you have *Acceptance Rate Blocking (ARB) turned on* in your market, *ARB should be replaced by DQO* which means ARB needs to be turned off *not to increase the risk level additionally* in a market and try to *keep the risk level the same*.
** If you *don’t have ARB* in your market, then your *local teams need to create a business case for showing that they need DQO in their market* and *need to pitch this business case to the reclass committee (management is part of it)* to *get an approval* for such a risky feature.
* Action points for you would be to read through the assessment, understand it and find out if you have ARB in SE and then follow our recommendation based on the outcome.

Hi [~accountid:712020:62d2d09a-02e2-437d-abbd-86f5be2b5737] 

I am of the opinion that we are free to introduce waiting fee as described in the ticket, without obligation to introduce changes to the T&Cs, provided that the amount:

#  will not exceed maximum amounts indicated in applicable resolutions regarding maximum prices for taxi services;
# will be visible in the app.

*Overview*

* *Clause 4.7 of the T&Cs directly indicates possibility to apply the waiting fee* “_Gdy kierowca przyjedzie na miejsce i wyśle powiadomienie o swoim przybyciu, aplikacja Bolt może rozpocząć naliczanie opłaty za oczekiwanie według stawek określonych w aplikacji Bolt_.”
* Additionally, clause 1.3. mentions that the total fee may include additional fees “_(…) Opłaty mogą uwzględniać inne należne opłaty, opłaty drogowe lub opłaty dodatkowe, w tym opłaty rezerwacyjne, opłaty miejskie, opłaty lotniskowe lub opłaty za przetwarzanie płatności podzielonych. (…)_”
* *The amount of waiting fee should not exceed maximum amounts indicated in applicable resolutions regarding maximum prices for taxi services*, e.g. in Warsaw it is PLN 50 per hour which would require from us setting a maximum waiting fee as PLN 0,83 per minute.
* *The maximum amount should be applicable to all categories*, meaning that the above amount per minute would apply both to economy and premium category.
* I do not believe that we should do anything before introducing the waiting fee because, as mentioned, T&Cs allow us to apply this fee. Of course, the team should focus on providing relevant information about the waiting fee in the app but this can be made based on other countries where the fee has been already in force, [e.g. Spain|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1x0Bmufaqrm8-ABn4nzJmDLDmXJ3DkR-AZo8bcLzNOcg/edit?gid=1625058149#gid=1625058149].

[~accountid:712020:0641ea87-e832-482b-8673-ab85e9ad6441] basicamente, antigamente os incentivos para os motoristas ao serviço de frotas tomavam como alvo a cidade onde a frota estava inscrita, pelo que algumas frotas optaram por criar várias frotas (no fundo a mesma empresa, em várias cidades). Ou apenas por serem frotas muito grandes que logisticamente davam preferencia a este tipo de operação (exemplo bluwalk).Pontos importantes:

# A Bolt nunca requisitou que a frota se inscrevesse em várias cidades para que lá pudesse operar, foi sempre uma decisão da frota fazê-lo.
# Um carro pode andar em qualquer região, independentemente da cidade de registo.
# O problema dos bónus/campanhas já foi resolvido, pelo que não há nenhum "senão" de manter uma cidade de registo e carros com atividade em várias cidades

*Se a frota criou duas frotas (uma em cada cidade) por opção* e registou o mesmo carro em ambas, temos que bloquear o carro onde este não tem atividade (não pode estar activo em Lisboa e no Algarve ao mesmo tempo, muito menos em duas frotas ao mesmo tempo).Para simplificar, podemos manter a opção de manter a base de operação numa única cidade, ter todos os carros e drivers nessa única frota e os drivers/carros andam livremente pelo país (sem ser necessário informar-nos) pois todos os registos de carros são únicos.

Adicionalmente, a frota simplesmente assumiu que o carro não poderia trabalhar em diferentes cidades e tinha de nos informar, mas esse não é o caso. Eles não têm de mudar nada num veículo para ele poder trabalhar noutra cidade.

Hi [~accountid:5bdbfc9b359ddf204e8c7e02] and [~accountid:61cb1160f3037f0069a4cb9e] to be honest then I got a bit lost with Denis' last message. My feedback here would be that Virtual Store as it is presented in the powerpoint is seen as an advertisement in the meaning of DSA if:

# it is an artificial virtual store meaning it is created only to *promote* specific merchant’s  *specific branded* products. At the same time the same merchant also has its “real” store on the Bolt platform selling the same products in addition to other products, 
# merchant or the brand owner pays directly or indirectly for Bolt for promoting these brand specific products under this artificial store. 

For me it seems that above mentioned requirements are fulfilled for the Virtual Store concept, meaning it is seen as an ad under the DSA and hence transparency obligation also applies for it. This means we have to:

# make it clear that the information is an advertisement through a prominent markings;
# disclose ​​the natural or legal person on whose behalf the advertisement is presented;
# disclose meaningful information directly and easily accessible from the advertisement about the main parameters used to determine the recipient to whom the advertisement is presented and, where applicable, about how to change those parameters.
