Hey [~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d] and [~accountid:5dcebc6199e7ea0c60b0f56c]! Need your input on this one, see below! 

For 🚗[ Driver: I want to delete my account|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360010217173#request-to-delete-drivers-account], *Portugal* uses a different undocumented process compared to *Global* to prevent fraud. 

“🌍 *Global process:*

* Go to the driver's profile in *Admin Panel* (Rides > Partners > Edit) and change the current status to _Deleted_ and click _Save_ at the bottom.
* In *Admin* tick _GDPR:_ _Driver deletion request_ label and click _Save_
** If you don't see this label, go to [GDPR: Driver deletion label not visible in Admin|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360010217173#gdpr-driver-deletion-label-not-visible-in-admin]
* Leave a comment on the profile: _Deletion request as of (enter date) + Beehive case link_ and save the comment”

However, the process for the *Portuguese* market is:

* “Admin Driver profile > Change “Status” from “Active” to “Hidden” > Add a comment with the beehive link.
* In *Admin* tick _GDPR:_ _Driver deletion request_ label and click _Save_
** If you don't see this label, go to [GDPR: Driver deletion label not visible in Admin|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360010217173#gdpr-driver-deletion-label-not-visible-in-admin]
* Leave a comment on the profile: _Deletion request as of (enter date) + Beehive case link_ and save the comment“



--

So Portugal hides the Driver profile, instead of deleting the Partner profile. *Their reasoning*:

The reasoning for the different process is that we noticed a pattern where drivers ask for account deletion to clear their records (fraud, quality, safety), by creating a new partner account after with a different email/phone.

*Why the duplication with the deleted partner is not found?* We have too much deleted partners accounts (+150.000), prior to 2023 we wouldn’t copy driver accounts, instead we created new partners every time there was a fleet change.
It is impossible for us to make this cross check.

Since 2023, a driver has only 1 partner account, he cannot be separated from it, and we track all his info at partner level. If we follow the current guideline, we’ll see fraudulent, aggressive drivers being able to avoid hardblocks and even getting unblocked, as we’ve seen in the past before implementing this process.

--

Context for the 1st case: The [order|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-order/orders/193513282?cityId=1] was picked up first, but the courier got stuck at the second provider, waiting for the order for approximately 20 minutes. During this time, the ETA only increased via the 3-minute threshold due to a lack of input.
*Causes*:
           • *First Cause:* Not updating all orders in a batch during event handling for one of the orders (this only occurs in certain edge cases).
               ◦ *Example:* Consider the Order Pickup event for the second order with a queue like [P2, D2, D1]. The current logic does not update the ETA for order 1.
               ◦ *Solution:* To ensure alignment with the recent Eater Revamp updates, we need to discuss which courier events require are deemed the best candidates for fixes to guarantee updates for all orders in a batch. Would recommend a discussion with Orchestration about possible batch cases.
           • *Second Cause:* Not updating batching activities in the {{cron job}} with the data received from Orchestration.
               ◦ Only active activities are updated based on courier travel estimates from Orchestration.
               ◦ Additionally, there is no logic for updating {{COURIER_PRE_GOING_TO_CLIENT}} and {{COURIER_PRE_GOING_TO_PROVIDER}}.
               ◦ In the above case, {{COURIER_PRE_GOING_TO_CLIENT}} was the active state, so no actual state update occurred.
               ◦ *Solution:* Begin updating these two states ({{COURIER_PRE_GOING_TO_CLIENT}} and {{COURIER_PRE_GOING_TO_PROVIDER}}) in the event of a batch by using the pickup/delivery estimations of the 1st order in the batch for the 2nd order states.

** STATUS * (tbc)*

* *Description of incident*:
** In short, a UK rider (Joachim Grundin) is concerned about 5 trips they did not take on 20 September between 2:00 and 4:00.
** On 1 October (12:10), rider [reported|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/447731486] a trip that they did not take. User demanded to know who was in the car.
*** On 4 October, another [report|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/449393603] (this time in Swedish) “_regarding five journeys made on the same day at the same time_… _The five journeys were made without my knowledge and without my identity being established_”. Trips were made in the UK.
*** Another [report|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/450936954] on 7 October (14:17).
*** User claims [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/449393603] that “_I want my £299 back that you have allowed your drivers to embezzle_”. As such, they appear to have suffered financial detriment. They also mention “_The trips in question were all made in London after midnight on 20 September_”.
** Bolt CS investigated and confirmed that the trip was ordered from the rider’s device. User was not happy - maintaining they had not taken the trip. They demanded to know “_How many reservations was made from my account between 02:00-04:00 am Sept 20?_”, threatening to go to the Swedish Press. User confirmed multiple trips from their account that they did not recognise (“_five trips during two hours with a total length of four hours_”).
*** User has stated “_There is a police report filed for this issue_” (they provided a reference number:5000-K1402119-22) and they have apparently engaged a lawyer. 
*** Unfortunately, this user was passed between many members of the support team and the matter has not been investigated properly.
* *Analysis*:
** Looking at rider’s account, the [trips|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A50%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22start_timestamp%22%3A1726679640%2C%22end_timestamp%22%3A1726959540%2C%22all_order_try_states%22%3Afalse%2C%22user_id%22%3A214545529%7D%7D&source_id=&city_id=&user_id=] were taken through their account (see [here|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/534504131/25?orderTryId=1019621922], [here|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/534507203/25?orderTryId=1019649852], [here|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/534508163/25?orderTryId=1019658739], and [here|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/534511091/25?orderTryId=1019678740]). This suggests this is not a case of a user getting emails relating to trips taken by another Bolt account. Assuming that the user still has access to the same account that the trips were taken on, this also suggests it is not a recycled phone number issue.
** Looking at account details history, no obvious changes around 20 September. Cannot see any clear signs of compromise.
** The user is not listed as part of the P1 login vulnerability incident.
* *Next Steps*:
** Ask CS to confirm:
*** Is this definitely a UK user? Why are they threatening the _Swedish_ press?
*** Does the user currently have access to their account? (If so, then it seems very unlikely that the account was hacked). Are they messaging us in-app (presumably they are), or via email?
*** Does their account show any signs of compromise?
*** Are there any other Bolt accounts with the user’s email address?

Hi [~accountid:712020:9c263122-6bc1-4bbe-91d7-c80d616c4514] ! Please see the answers below:

* *What categories of data would be made available?*

*Personal Information* meaning information relating to an identifiable, living, natural person, and where it is applicable, an identifiable, existing juristic person. This includes but is not limited to:

* information relating to the race, gender, sex, pregnancy, marital status, national, ethnic or social origin, colour, sexual orientation, age, physical or mental health, well-being, disability, religion, conscience, belief, culture, language and birth of the person;
* information relating to the education or the medical, financial, criminal or employment history of employees;
* any identifying number, symbol, e-mail address, physical address, telephone number, location information, online identifier or other particular assignment to employees;
* the biometric information of employees;
* the personal opinions, views or preferences of employees;
* correspondence sent by the person that is implicitly or explicitly of a private or confidential nature or further correspondence that would reveal the contents of the original correspondence; and
* the views or opinions of another individual about employees.

*Special personal information* i.e. personal information about the following:

* Race (like where a company submits reports to the Department of Labour where the statistical information must be recorded)
* Ethnic origin
* Trade union membership
* Health (like where you apply for an insurance policy)
* Biometric information (like to verify your identity); and / or your criminal behaviour and alleged commission of an offense



* *Which entity would be making the data available (the data flow)? Will it be from us to them? If so, will the data be sent from a local entity or Bolt OU?*

Bolt Services ZA & Bolt OU will predominantly be responsible for making the data available to Strata-g. Our understanding is that the data will be sent from a local entity however, it may also be sent from Bolt OU.

Strata-g also provides a monthly breakdown of hours or services renders which includes personal information received from Bolt and/or obtained during the course of an investigation, disciplinary hearing or legal processes such as Conciliation and Arbitration.

 

* *How will that data be made available?*

Strata-g collects personal information from the payroll or HR departments of Bolt when they capture financial and non-financial information

Strata-g collects information about you based on your use of our services

Strata-g collects information about you based on how you engage or interact with us such as via our support desk, emails, letters, telephone calls and surveys

Strata-g collects personal information from completed forms i.e. contact information, billing information, membership application forms, etc.

 

* *Do they utilise any sub-processors - third party processors/ cloud storage services?*

Whilst Strata-g does not utilise any third-party payment processors, we do utilise cloud storage services.

* The obligations regarding personal data breach notifications are outlined in the [Personal Data Protection Act|https://www.riigiteataja.ee/en/eli/523012019001/consolide]. Specifically, Article 44 establishes the obligation to notify the AKI (Estonian Data Protection Inspectorate) and details the conditions under which such notification is required.



!Screenshot 2024-10-14 at 11.56.05.png|width=1437,height=859,alt="Screenshot 2024-10-14 at 11.56.05.png"!

 

*§ 44. Notification of Personal Data Breach to the Estonian Data Protection Inspectorate*

# Controllers must notify the Estonian Data Protection Inspectorate of a personal data breach _likely to risk individuals' rights within 72 hours_ of becoming aware of it.
# Processors must promptly inform controllers of any data breaches.
# Notifications must include:
#* Details of the breach (nature, categories of data subjects, and affected data).
#* Contact information for the data protection officer.
#* Potential consequences of the breach.
#* Measures taken to address the breach and mitigate its impact.
# If notified after 72 hours, reasons for the delay must be provided.
# Breaches involving data from other EU Member States must be communicated to the relevant controller without delay.
# Controllers must document all personal data breaches, including their circumstances and remedial actions taken. 

* The additional guidelines as well as links to the data breach notification forms can be found [here|https://www.aki.ee/meist/vota-uhendust/rikkumisteade#esita-rikkumisteade-]. But these guidelines do not provide any additional information beyond what has already been outlined in Article 44.
* No specific cases on recycled numbers was found [here|https://www.aki.ee/meist/teadlikkus/kohtulahendid].
* Additional information for other EEA countries can be found [here|https://www.edpb.europa.eu/notify-data-breach_es].

deployed in prod, already automation working and above are the initial numbers/updates on MinuDoc access.

*Assessment for RO:*
Used resource: [Bolt Plus questionnaire for RO|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1p3HUnj2m1-vVUA60-K5zw2QacNpoHy8p/edit]

*Feature itself*

# Legitimacy of a feature is mainly subject to whether it may bring any complications stemming from commerce related laws. If Commerce Legal has reviewed it and said there are no problems - it should be fine. They should assess it from local perspective too because they prohibit GFT counsels to take advice from local counsels. Therefore, GFT counsel should mainly assess consumer protection aspect.
# Is feature beneficial for consumers? If yes, they are less inclined to complain. The feature is definitely beneficial from consumer perspective.

*Changes to T&Cs*

# We are changing the scope of the benefit. However, we add benefits without removing or substituting other benefits, which benefits consumers.
# Do our T&Cs outline benefits that we offer? No, benefits are only described in the app, therefore, we don't need to add the change to the T&Cs, but need to describe the new benefit in the app.
# What T&Cs say about updates to benefits? Clause 5 states: "Bolt reserves the right to change Bolt Plus Benefits, Subscription Fee and other applicable conditions at its sole discretion. *Significant changes to the Bolt Plus subscription Benefits and/or Bolt Plus Subscription Fee increase will only apply from the next billing cycle after auto-renewal*. Bolt will always notify you about any significant changes to the Bolt Plus Benefits, other conditions and/or these Terms via email in advance of the next billing cycle and auto-renewal", It means if we consider this benefit a "signifiant change" we need to 1) inform customers; 2) apply change only from the next billing cycle.
# Is this change significant? Yes, it is an addition of a new benefit.
# Would consumer suffer if we do not inform them about the change? They would benefit from knowing about new benefit, but will not suffer in case we apply it and not tell them. However, the best practice is still to notify.
# Should we apply it from the next billing cycle? Applying it form the next billing cycle would be disadvantageous to consumers, but otherwise, we will be in breach of our T&Cs.
# *Conclusion:* need to notify about new benefit, which shall apply from the next billing cycle, but no need to amend T&Cs.

*Romanian specific issues:*

# Changing the characteristics of a product or service unilaterally, without the customer’s agreement would constitute an abusive clause under Law no. 193/2000 on abusive clauses in contracts concluded between consumers and professionals (“Law 193/2000”) and transposing Directive 93/13/CEE. (Comment of the external counsel: The consumer must be given a prior notice before the new conditions enter into force, in order to be able to cancel the subscription. The scope for this is that the consumer is not charged more/offered less automatically, without having had the possibility to opt-out.)
## The change we are going to introduce is beneficial to consumers i.e. the scope of what they are getting is not less than before. However, notification would be beneficial from legal/marketing perspective, but there is no defined notification period, i.e. we need to notify as soon as reasonably possible before making changes.
# According to the Romanian consumer protection and court practice, the characteristics of a product or service (which cannot be changed without the consumer’s approval) are those taken into consideration upon taking the buying decision.
## Could this feature be of such importance that it would motivate someone to buy the subscription to Bolt Plus? Yes, this is totally possible. Therefore, we should notify the consumers about the change, however, there is no need to get their approval by accepting updated T&Cs, because we should apply benefit from the next billing cycle and this will allow consumers to withdraw from subscriptions before change comes into force.

*Using cashback benefit for rh in rides campaigns*

* Need more information on how exactly it will be working, but by the end of the day this is more in the domain of Commerce Legal.
* [Rules of contests organised by Bolt on Social Media|https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/regulament-social-media/?category=rides] - have nothing that would prevent from using cashback as a reward. Standard T&Cs templates for campaigns in RO also do not have any limitations for offering such prize. The only requirement is to describe eligibility properly - for example, whether user has to be subscribed to Bolt Plus to receive the benefit.



*Summary for the business*
GFT counsel assessed the legitimacy of the benefit only from the consumer protection perspective since other aspects were assessed by Commerce Legal (financial regulations) and Privacy Team (data protection). The conclusion is that the benefit can be added as it benefits the consumer. When adding the benefit we don’t need to change Bolt Plus T&Cs, but according to Clause 5 of our Bolt Plus T&Cs and local regulations related to consumer protection we need to:

# Notify the consumer as soon as possible about introduction of a new benefit before the benefit is introduced, but there is no specific timeframe for such notification.
# Describe the new benefit in the app - what are the conditions for getting the benefit (if any), how does it work, any limitations.
# Benefit can only be introduced to active users from the next billing period, because the benefit is considered to be significant and capable of influencing consumers' decision making regarding purchasing the subscription. The risk of consumer complaints is lower due to change being beneficial to consumers, but introducing benefit immediately will be contrary to our Bolt Plus T&Cs and we will be in breach of our obligations.

Implications regarding giving bolt balance credit back as incentives for ride hailing in rides campaigns should be assessed by Commerce Legal. From consumer protection perspective there are no obstacles as long as campaign T&Cs clearly describe eligibility to such prize - for example, whether user has to be subscribed to Bolt Plus to receive the benefit, any time or other limitations on claiming the prize, etc.

Please note that if benefit is later to be removed you will need to inform customers in advance (the earlier the better) and will be able to remove it only at the end of the billing period (i.e. change will be effective only with the next billing period). Such change would require approval of the consumer and decision to renew the subscription can be considered as consent as long as consumer was notified about change of benefits in advance.

Over the past few years, there has been an increase in the number of enforcements and decisions passed by the national data protection supervisory authority, the Information and Data Protection Commissioner (IDPC or “Commissioner”) in Malta, in connection with infringements of data protection law.

The majority of the decisions published relate mainly to *an infringement of the data subjects’ rights* to their personal data in terms of Article 15 – as well as Articles 16 and 17 – of the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and to the *unlawful processing of personal data* pursuant to Article 6 of the GDPR.

Source [link|https://practiceguides.chambers.com/practice-guides/data-protection-privacy-2024/malta/trends-and-developments]. 

While specific phishing-related fines may not be frequently reported, the underlying issues of insufficient security measures, as mandated by Article 32 of the GDPR, are indeed a prevalent violation. (I haven’t found any huge phishing-related fine in Malta). 

*Regulatory authorities frequently cite failures in this area when imposing fines,* *highlighting the lack of effective safeguards against unauthorized access and data breaches, because phishing often exploits insufficient security measures,* *leading to breaches where personal data is compromised*. According to various reports, such as those from the DLA Piper GDPR Fines and Data Breach Survey, insufficient technical and organizational measures have been a common basis for fines across the EEA ​([International|https://cms.law/en/int/publication/gdpr-enforcement-tracker-report/numbers-and-figures], [Global Law Firm | DLA Piper|https://www.dlapiper.com/en-gb/insights/publications/2024/01/dla-piper-gdpr-fines-and-data-breach-survey-january-2024]).

The list of most famous cases where Article 32 was violated is [here|https://www.enforcementtracker.com/]. 
The fines for violations (including violation of Article 32) range from EUR 4,000.00 -  EUR4,500,00.00.

Hey, [~accountid:712020:bba87790-3d07-4531-9af3-f5df86d0d56a]! Here is the assessment for *RO* market:

GFT counsel assessed the legitimacy of the benefit only from the consumer protection perspective since other aspects were assessed by Commerce Legal (financial regulations) and Privacy Team (data protection). The conclusion is that the benefit can be added as it benefits the consumer. When adding the benefit we don’t need to change our current Bolt Plus T&Cs, but according to Clause 5 of our Bolt Plus T&Cs and local regulations related to consumer protection we need to:

# Notify the consumer as soon as possible about introduction of a new benefit before the benefit is introduced, but there is no specific timeframe for such notification.
# Describe the new benefit in the app - what are the conditions for getting the benefit (if any), how does it work, any limitations.
# Benefit can only be introduced to active subscribers from the next billing period, because the benefit is considered to be significant and capable of influencing consumers' decision making regarding purchasing the subscription. The risk of consumer complaints is lower due to change being beneficial to consumers, but introducing benefit immediately will be contrary to our Bolt Plus T&Cs and we will be in breach of our obligations.

Please note that if benefit is later to be removed you will need to inform customers in advance (the earlier the better) and will be able to remove it only at the end of the billing period (i.e. change will be effective only from the next billing period). Such change would require approval of the consumer and decision to renew the subscription can be considered as consent as long as consumer was notified about change of benefits in advance.

Implications regarding giving bolt balance credit back as incentives for ride hailing in rides campaigns should be assessed by Commerce Legal. From consumer protection perspective there are no obstacles as long as campaign T&Cs clearly describe eligibility to such prize - for example, whether user has to be subscribed to Bolt Plus to receive the benefit, any time or other limitations on claiming the prize, etc.

short answer: 

including start and end addresses on invoices helps us to meet customer needs, ensures legal and tax compliance, reduces potential disputes, and maintains competitiveness in the market. Failing to do so may lead to customer dissatisfaction, lost business, and increased administrative costs.



long answer:

h3. Impacts of Including Start and End Addresses on the Invoice:

# *Improved Customer Experience and Trust*:
#* *Transparency*: Including detailed trip data (start and end addresses) enhances transparency for users. This is especially important for business travelers who need precise records for expense reports or tax declarations.
#* *Record-Keeping*: Business users often need detailed travel logs to track expenses and maintain mileage records for tax deductions or internal expense reimbursement. By providing start and end locations, we ensure that customers can easily submit these details without needing to track them manually.
#* *Reduced Disputes*: Clear invoicing with detailed trip data reduces the likelihood of disputes or confusion over billing, as customers can easily verify the routes and times of travel.
# *Legal and Tax Compliance for Customers*:
#* *Supporting Tax Documentation*: In many countries, tax authorities require detailed documentation of business expenses for deductions. If a user is claiming carsharing expenses for tax purposes, the invoice must show trip-specific information such as dates, distances, and locations. Without start and end addresses, the invoice may not meet legal requirements for tax audits or expense reports, which could lead to penalties or rejected claims for the customer.
#* *Audit Readiness*: By including start and end addresses, the mobility provider helps business users be ready for any potential tax audits. An incomplete invoice may cause issues for companies if they cannot justify the business use of carsharing trips, potentially leading to denied tax deductions or additional tax liabilities.
# *Administrative Efficiency*:
#* *Less Manual Work for Users*: If the invoice includes all necessary details, users won’t need to manually record start and end addresses for their own expense reporting. This reduces the administrative burden on customers, making the service more attractive, especially for business travelers who need fast and efficient solutions.
#* *Automatic Logbook Generation*: Many businesses require employees to submit logbooks or trip records for reimbursement purposes. By providing start and end addresses on the invoice, we can essentially create an automatic logbook for the user, making it easier for the customer to integrate the data into their expense management systems.

h3. Why Do We Need to Show the Start and End Address?

# *Tax and Regulatory Requirements*:
#* In many jurisdictions, businesses and individuals who claim tax deductions or reimbursements for transportation expenses need to provide evidence that the travel was for business purposes. This usually requires detailed information on the trip, including start and end locations, to demonstrate that the trip was necessary for business.
#* Regulatory bodies might require transport providers to maintain accurate records of all trips taken by customers, including start and end points, to prevent fraud or misuse of the service.
# *Customer Expectations and Market Competitiveness*:
#* Competitors may already offer more detailed invoicing. If we fail to offer the same, we risk losing customers who require these details for tax and business reporting. By including the start and end addresses, we can meet the needs of business travelers and avoid falling behind in the market.

h3. What Happens If We Don’t Include Start and End Addresses?

# *Customer Dissatisfaction*:
#* Business customers could be frustrated by the lack of essential details on the invoice, leading to dissatisfaction and potentially causing them to switch to a competitor that provides more complete invoices. The lack of detailed information creates extra work for customers, who then need to manually track and verify trips.
# *Increased Risk of Errors in Reporting*:
#* Without the start and end addresses, customers might struggle to accurately complete their tax declarations or travel expense reports. This could result in errors, rejected claims, or audits. Businesses might have a harder time substantiating carsharing costs as a legitimate business expense without proper documentation.
# *Lost Tax Deductions or Compliance Penalties*:
#* In some cases, users might be unable to claim certain trips as business expenses without clear location data. For businesses, this can result in lost tax deductions and increased tax liabilities. In the worst-case scenario, a lack of proper documentation could lead to tax penalties or fines.
# *Higher Customer Support Costs*:
#* Without detailed trip data on the invoice, customers may contact our support team more frequently to request additional documentation or clarification. This increases our administrative burden and operational costs.

Hi [~accountid:5d91ad8a1d47a50c34d48412] 

# *Limitation of working hours*: Just in case that there isn’t any misunderstanding: under law, the limitation on working hours should be implemented by the employer (or a person giving tasks to the minor under a service agreement). This means that technically Bolt is not obligated under law to see to it that the minor does not exceed these limits. However, my logic is that since Bolt’s and the minor’s contractual relationship may fall under the eye of the supervisor, it would be to the advantage of all parties if Bolt had these safeguards in place.
+To give a more specific answer to your question+: These time limits should be read as a prohibition for the employer to demand and/or agree to any more hours or work from the minor. Therefore adding a technical solution is not critical in my opinion.
Furthermore, if Bolt were to implement the time limits as “hard” restrictions, there is risk that Bolt would be seen even more as an employer – it would be difficult to argue that Bolt does not see itself as an employer but nevertheless follows some employment regulations. 
The time limits should therefore be as informative/suggestive – it should not be seen that Bolt is implementing this as a perceived obligation from the law.
# *Parental consent*: The law does not state in what form is the consent supposed to be. However, for clarity and documentation purposes I strongly suggest to have it in written form (same way as for Lithuania).
Regarding birth certificates, there is no specific legal provision that demands this. However, neither is there a legal provision that grants Bolt the right to assume that the parent/guardian can represent the minor. This means that should it turn out that the person who gave their “consent” did so illegally, then it can be argued that Bolt was supposed to confirm their representative rights and is therefore “at fault”. In Estonia the market practice seems to be asking for the birth certificate or another document that proves the legal guardianship (this is done, for example, in hospitals and also in the airport).

{{container_memory_working_set_bytes = RSS + active cache}}

Since *inactive cache* (which isn't counted in the working set) is already excluded, when dropping caches, the reduction comes directly from *active cache* and so it is expected that {{container_memory_working_set_bytes}} reduces.

Some [sources|https://mohamedmsaeed.medium.com/memory-working-set-vs-memory-rss-in-kubernetes-which-one-you-should-monitor-8ef77bf0acee] suggest in addition to monitor  and alert on {{container_memory_rss}} which is the amount of anonymous and swap cache memory. However, it could introduce additional noise due to alerts being triggered when containers are not under significant memory pressure, as cached memory (tracked in {{working_set_bytes}}) could still be reclaimable.

What is agreed upon is that {{container_memory_working_set_bytes}} is tracked by the OOM killer, and so best practice is to monitor and alert using this metric as a minimum. Similarly, kubectl top and k9s use this metric.

We have a legal obligation according to the RO legislation (the RH law) to share data about the operators with the Fiscal Agency. That in addition to the Fiscal procedure laws.

We’ve been doing this for quite some time (the law entered into force in 2019) and as you can see in the ticket link above, we are under lots of pressure. 

So yes, the Fiscal Authority is usually requesting info based on the Fiscal Law and in addition, we are forced to provide information according to *GEO 49/2019*:

Art. 26. -

*At the request of the authorities with powers in the field, provided by this emergency ordinance, the operator of the digital platform or the branch of the non-resident operator of the digital platform, as the case may be, will make available to them all the required information that it holds in relation to the performance of the activity by the operators of alternative transport through the digital platform. The provision of this information is carried out in accordance with the legal provisions in force*.

Art. 29. -

(1) The control of compliance with the provisions of this emergency ordinance is ensured by:

*c) National Fiscal Administration Agency*;

(3) At the headquarters of the operator of the digital platform or of the branch of the non-resident operator of the digital platform in Romania and/or of the alternative transport operator, the control of the alternative transport is carried out by the representatives of the authorities mentioned in para. (1) lit. a) -*c*), e) and f).

*So information must be shared. Now in terms of volume and exact data, Privacy should decide of course, if the request is very extensive.*

There are two reasons why this happens:

# There is an issue with cleaning up stale connections which are dropped by the DB server (or ProxySQL) itself – we seem to ignore this event and the connections stay in the pool. Then once a DB query is done, such connection is picked up from the pool and a ping is sent on this connection. It times out after 5 seconds, since the connection is closed, and then the new connection is created instead. This only appears for services which have an extremely low amount of traffic, such as {{chaos-testing-notification}} which is responsible for sending the notifications, or {{central-scheduler}} which is responsible for scheduling the notifications for a future session.
The discussion of the issue is here: [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C046TK6FZ7Z/p1726139576777419|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C046TK6FZ7Z/p1726139576777419|smart-link] 
We have discussed it with Juri last and decided that someone should reproduce this issue locally to confirm it, but I’m not aware if anything was done in this direction. The reproduction strategy is to set up {{wait_timeout}} for local TiDB or MySQL Docker container to a small value, run literally any service which does DB calls and make two requests with an interval larger than {{wait_timeout}}. Technically, setting {{wait_timeout}} to a low value shouldn’t cause any issues, just more frequent recycling of connections in the pool.
# There are no retries in {{chaos-testing}} flows, most importantly in the “create session” flow for scheduling the notifications (via IRC calls to {{central-scheduler}}) and for sending notifications in-place or based on {{central-scheduler}} events (both sent as IRC calls to {{chaos-testing-notification}}). The event handling is also using fire-and-forget, this was a decision that we made to reduce the scope and complexity of the initial implementation.

I would argue that fixing the connection issue would be a much more beneficial solution and would also help for other extra low usage services (which PINT happens to own).

Hi [~accountid:6256f19413c2c8006a365659] 

GDPR is the primary regulation for data protection in the EU. According to Article 87, processing the numbers on the back of ID cards is only permitted if there’s a clear legal basis. EU countries may have specific rules, but generally, collecting the back of an ID card is discouraged unless absolutely necessary. The GDPR emphasizes *data minimization*, meaning only essential data for verification should be collected.

If a Thai user is traveling in Europe and requires verification, it’s best to follow *the principle of data minimization.* Since the back of the Thai ID card is not essential for identity verification, collecting it could risk non-compliance with both GDPR and Thailand’s PDPA. 

Avoiding this collection would not only ensure legal compliance but also simplify engineering work by maintaining a consistent approach, regardless of location.

Please let me know if you need further clarification.

Thank you very much.

* *voluntary rider verification (pic+ID)*
** Voluntary rider verification is rolled out in some of the EU countries that have the same privacy law (GDPR) as Romania, so we would not be opposed to this.
* *mandatory rider verification based on negative signals*
** What “negative signals” do you have in mind? Do we have a definite list?

** At this point, we don’t have any mandatory rider verification rolled out in any of the EU countries for safety reasons, and it was not on our team’s radar that such initiative might come. I would strongly advise against rolling this out without proper analysis.

I understand the seriousness of the case in Romania, and while we will assist you as much as possible, we must be careful with rollout of certain features, as Bolt is currently under the radar of privacy regulators in several countries, and therefore we must be careful to not implement any features that are in direct breach of the privacy laws, or else we are risking of receiving a fine / suspension of features on EU level.

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 14 September 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled, in particular:

*Your rights*

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. As we understood, this is out of our responsabilites as a platform and it should be done by the fleets. The only thing we can do is educate the riders and ask them to reach out to the fleets. But how can they reach out to the fleets if they don’t have their contact details anywhere? We cannot give them the contact details as that would mean a GDPR breach. 

In this case, it would be best to make the contact details of the fleet available for the users, at least the email address of the fleet if not the phone number, so they can have someone to write directly instead of contacting us and basically get no help.

“““

Long story short - from time to time it's still possible to make a business order if preauth for it has failed.
This happens if Rides reuse same search token for new preparePayment call, and on our side we had a logic that if {{topup_auth}} for same order already exists - just allow the order without checking for its status.
Once a company has unpaid debt and user will try to make an order - order normally is being rejected even earlier (after calling {{checkPaymentAllowedForCompany}} from business-user). But at this moment we are also attempting to capture the debt and if you catch the timing and place an order very quickly while we are processing this "debt topup" - same scenario from 1st paragraph is applied if same order_id will be used.

So as a fix I've decided to do the following:

* (1st idea - rejected) - check status of existing preauth and fail the order if it's failed. This won't work when you really topped up your card balance, and want to retry the order (while somehow having same search_token)
* instead of that we'll create new preauthorization (same {{topup_auth.order_key}} but that's fine) and rely on the response of a new one. So if you'll pay all your debts and topup the card you'll be able to book an order with a new successful preauth

* Cargoson operate an aggregation platform of delivery services. Their clients then opt in to which delivery partner they wish to use when using the Cargoson platform (for example using Bolt Send) 
* Cargoson will connect to our Ride Booker API and will offer Bolt Send as an option to their clients. 
* If their clients would like to use Bolt Send, they will need to create a Bolt Business account with us, in order for us to open up a credit line. This mean all billing for our services (whilst delivered by Cargoson) would be managed directly with their customers, in turn becoming our customers. 
* When a customer opens a Bolt Business Account, we would need to also create a Ride Booker Account to generate the unique API access token, to allow Cargoson to connect to the specific client account 
** This is what we need to solve. In theory by creating a Ride Booker Account and allowing access to generate the Ride Booker API tokens, we need protection with their clients as to limit abuse of the live connectivity they could have access too
** One solution I would propose is that whilst their clients create a Bolt Business account with us, the Ride Booker Account connected to the Business Account is actually in the name of the Cargoson tech team, who are bound by the terms in this agreement. 
** So the hierachy would be individual business accounts for each client, and individual Ride Booker account connected to the Business Accounts, accessed only by Cargoson 

Can we have a review of the above and decide if this is feasible?

Hi,

This request comes from the Economic Crime Investigation Service (Romanian Police) regarding a *criminal file on tax evasion*. 

The ride-hailing law - GEO 49/2019 does not seem to cover them, see below:

_Art. 29. -_

_(1) The control of compliance with the provisions of this emergency ordinance is ensured by:_

_a) Ministry of Communications and Information Society;_

_b) State Inspectorate for Road Transport Control - I.S.C.T.R.;_

_c) National Fiscal Administration Agency;_

*_d) agents and police officers designated as traffic policemen within the Romanian Police_*_;_

_e) National Authority for Consumer Protection;_

_f) territorial labour inspectorates, according to the normative acts that regulate the field of competence of these institutions._

_(2) In road traffic, the control of alternative transport is carried out by the representatives of the authorities mentioned in para. (1) lit. b)-_*_d)._*

_(3) At the headquarters of the operator of the digital platform or of the branch of the non-resident operator of the digital platform in Romania and/or of the alternative transport operator, the control of the alternative transport is carried out by the representatives of the authorities mentioned in para. (1) lit. a) -c), e) and f)._

*Hence, they are sending this request based on other laws.* 

The Ordinance cites the following laws:

*1. Law no. 241/2005 for preventing and combating tax evasion*:
_Art. 9 (1) The following acts committed for the purpose of evading the fulfilment of fiscal obligations constitute tax evasion crimes and are punishable by imprisonment from 3 to 10 years and the prohibition of certain rights or a fine: (…)_
_b) the omission, in whole or in part, of highlighting, in the accounting documents or in other legal documents, the commercial operations performed or the incomes achieved;_

*2. The Criminal Code of 2009*
_Art. 35. - (1) The offence is continued when a person commits at different intervals of time, but in the implementation of the same resolution, actions or inactions that present, each separately, the content of the same offence._
_Art. 5. - (1) If one or more criminal laws have intervened from the commission of the crime to the final judgment of the case, the more favorable law shall be applied._
_(2) The provisions of para. (1) also applies to normative acts or their provisions declared unconstitutional, as well as to emergency ordinances approved by Parliament with amendments or additions or rejected, if during the time they were in force they contained more favourable criminal provisions._

The Ordinance mentions that "_documents in Bolt's possession are needed to solve the case_"

*(they refer to Bolt Services RO SRL, which is the local entity and which, according to the licensing documents in Romania, “_has the right/obligation to make available to the public institutions, in accordance with their competences, the data relating to journey, route, passengers, drivers, transport operators, car, location, contracts etc_”).

The Ordinance also mentions that the request is made based on *art. 170 of the 2010 Criminal Procedure Code*: _(1) If there is a reasonable suspicion regarding the preparation or commission of a crime and there are grounds to believe that an object or document can serve as evidence in the case, the criminal investigation body or the court may order the natural or legal person in whose possession they are to present and hand them over, subject to taking evidence_.

*So, it seems that the laws give them the right to ask us for this data, wdyt* [~accountid:712020:9f38c9c2-43a9-46c6-9106-86ff0d35ba24] [~accountid:712020:8c797c70-7a57-496e-aa3f-5d91df806eb2] *. But I would assume that it is up to Privacy to decide if the volume of data exceeds the data protection regulations in force.*

Hey, [~accountid:712020:13033e65-435c-4794-a380-e007eba7615a]! Thank you for looping me in and sorry for the delayed reply.

My understanding is that obligation to share information with the relevant authority is stated in Article 26 of the GEO 49/2019:

{quote}*At the request of the authorities* with powers in the field, provided for by this Emergency Ordinance, *the operator of the digital platform* or the branch of the non-resident operator of the digital platform, as the case may be, *shall make available to them all the required information it holds in relation to the activity of alternative transport operators through the digital platform*. {quote}

In Article 25 of the GEO 49/2019 we can see that one of the obligations of the platform (i.e. Bolt) is to admit to the platform only those drivers, who comply with the provisions of the GEO 49/2019:

{quote}*to admit to the digital platform* only passengers who have duly registered their personal data requested through the digital platform and *only alternative transport operators and drivers who comply with the provisions of this Emergency Ordinance*. {quote}

This in turn means that *drivers/alternative transport operators need to comply with the requirements set out in Article 23* *and that Bolt should somehow verify and hold information that proves that these drivers are compliant* with the requirements (we also should check whether they (*drivers*) and their *vehicles* are still compliant every 12 months according to Article 25 (k)). Requirements for the vehicles are set out in in Article 24.

Relevant for the request requirements set out in Article 23 are as follows:

{quote}b) to hold a certificate of attestation of professional training for the carriage of persons for hire issued by the Romanian Road Authority - A.R.R.{quote}

Relevant for the request requirements set out in Article 24 are as follows:

{quote}c) alternative transportation badge;

d) certified copy of the authorisation for alternative transport{quote}

According to the above Articles Bolt shall check and retain copies of the documents and therefore provide these to the requesting authority in accordance with Article 26.

In the request described in the ticket we are allegedly being requested to provide the following:

{quote}Professional ride-hailing driving certificate (front)

Professional ride-hailing driving certificate (back)

Car registration certificate

Compliant copy

ARR Sticker{quote}

A screenshot of the request would be helpful to verify the list of requested documents, however, as far as I understand we would be capable to provide: 

* a copy of the certificate of attestation of professional training for the carriage of persons for hire issued by the Romanian Road Authority (for the requested Professional ride-hailing driving certificate (front and back))
* a copy of the alternative transportation badge (potentially to cover Car registration certificate and Compliant copy)
* a certified copy of the authorisation for alternative transport (potentially to cover ARR Sticker)

This list of documents that we can provide is different from the documents requested because:

# Car registration certificate - is not requested under GEO 49/2019, however it should be provided if it is requested by [GEO 195/2002|https://legislatie.just.ro/Public/DetaliiDocument/74028] according to Article 24 (Article 10 of GEO 195/2002 prohibits driving on vehicles with suspended registration and Article 11 demands that owners of vehicles shall register their vehicles, so technically registration certificate is one of the required documents and we should provide it if we have it). However, according to Article 22 of GEO 49/2019 alternative transportation badge should contain car registration number and digital platforms (i.e. Bolt) shall keep a register of all alternative transport badges issued for carrying out alternative transport on its digital platform;
# Compliant copy - not sure what is meant by that, perhaps seeing the wording in Romanian would help to understand.
# ARR Sticker - same as above, but I assume it refers to a certified copy of the authorisation for alternative transport.

[~accountid:712020:13033e65-435c-4794-a380-e007eba7615a], I suggest that it could be helpful to see the original request of the authority (i.e. a screenshot or something of the request), try to verify what are “Compliant copy” and “ARR Sticker“ and provide the mentioned above documents as according to the GEO 49/2019 these are the documents that we should have and share upon request with the relevant authority.

Please let me know if you have any other questions.

I again emphasize that we may still want to meet their claim, out of good faith. This is because the claim is relatively small and it is not guaranteed that they won’t turn to court. If they do, it is not guaranteed that Bolt would win the case and even if Bolt does win the case, we would still have carried additional expenses and resources that could have been avoided.

It is therefore a business decision whether to double down and refuse to pay the claim, but risk with litigation (the success of which can’t be guaranteed), or to cut our losses and pay the claim.

If the decision is to refuse payment, then I advise to answer them along the following lines (+*PROVIDED THE AREA IN QUESTION IS PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE*+):

Bolt has not caused and is not liable for any damage to the owner. Firstly, no direct damage has been reported as a result of the scooters being parked on the property in question. Secondly, Bolt is not liable for the legal fees. This is explained as follows:

* The property has not been marked as private and the owner has not marked clear boundaries of the property. In addition, the owner has decided to make the property – and the entrance in particular – publicly accessible. The above means that the owner is expected to tolerate more interference of property than normal.
* Nevertheless, Bolt is always open to extend its no park zone in case it interferes with someone’s property – this is Bolt’s normal practice and is proven by the fact that Bolt extended the no park zone as soon as the initial request was received.
* The owner could have always contacted Bolt directly and thus avoid any legal fees. Bolt is not liable for the fact that the owner decided to use legal services when this was in fact unnecessary and unreasonable.
* There is no sufficient causal connection between Bolt’s scooters being parked on the owner’s property (which is publicly accessible) and the owner’s decision to take on legal fees – Bolt’s actions have had no affect on this decision.
* Furthermore, the § 1004 BGB referenced grants the owner the right to demand that the interference of property be removed. It does not grant the owner the right to demand payment of any alleged damages (which have not occurred in this case at all).

We should therefore ask that the owner once again take into account our initial compliance with their demand, and waive the unfounded claim for the legal fees which Bolt is not obligated to pay.

Hey, [~accountid:60f2a71843c956007065f2ad]! Thank you for your help and all the information. I have located this document containing provisions you referred to from the 2010 Criminal Procedure Code: [https://rai-see.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/New_Criminal_Procedure_Code_EN.pdf|https://rai-see.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/New_Criminal_Procedure_Code_EN.pdf]. I can see that Article 170 contains this important information:

{quote}(1) In the event that there is a *reasonable suspicion* in relation to the preparation or commission of an offense and *there are reasons to believe that an object or document can serve as evidence* in a case, the criminal investigation bodies or the court may order the natural person or legal entity holding them to provide and surrender them, subject to receiving proof of surrender.

(4) *An order* *by criminal investigation bodies* or a court resolution *has to contain*: the person having ordered the surrender, the name of the person having the obligation to surrender an object, document or computer data, a description of the object, document or computer data that need to be surrendered, as well as the date and place where they need to be surrendered.{quote}

We don’t know whether the suspicion of the investigation body is reasonable, but we can assess the following:

# Can the document serve as evidence? 
## They are investigating tax evasion. Can finished rides, ride duration, distance, kilometers, ride value, date, payment method (cash/card), driver’s name, and the car's registration number help to prove the offence being committed? In my opinion the relevant data would be number of finished rides, ride value, date, payment method - this is subject to Privacy team’s review.
# Did the order contain all relevant information? Yes, the order contained information about the requester, requestee, data requested, date and method of providing requested data.

Article 171 states that in case such information is not provided voluntarily:

{quote}criminal investigation bodies, through a prosecutorial order, or the court, through a court resolution, shall order their forced seizure.{quote}

This means that the disclosure is not mandatory per se, however, I believe that we nevertheless shall provide the information subject to reasonable limitations to comply with our obligations regarding data protection.

Hi, [~accountid:5d91ad8a1d47a50c34d48412]! Thank you for your patience. Please see the advice regarding onboarding couriers in Romania that are under the age of 18 (i.e. minors):

# *Minimum age:*
## Persons may be employed in Romania only after they are 16 years old (this is the age of legal working consent).
## Minors between 15 and 16 may be employed only with their parents consent.

# *Documentation:* 
## There are no special documents required to employ persons that are at least 16 years old, but consent from parents is required when persons of age 15 are employed.
## Bolt as a platform provider is not required to check any documents regarding couriers that are below of age 18 employed by fleets, however, it is recommended to:
### Impose an obligation on fleets to comply with all applicable legislation (this is already ensured by clause 4.2 of the General T&Cs (available here: [https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/tnc-delivery/?category=delivery|https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/tnc-delivery/?category=delivery|smart-link] );
### Add the additional requirement that the job was deemed by a certified work safety and security expert as suitable for a minor (more information in section 3 below).

# *Other requirements: Any further legal considerations or restrictions we should be aware of?*
## Our own General T&Cs limit age of the couriers that can provide their services on our Bolt Food Platform to 18 years (clause 2.4 of the General T&Cs (available here: [https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/tnc-delivery/?category=delivery|https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/tnc-delivery/?category=delivery|smart-link])). We need to amend our T&Cs to allow couriers of a younger age to be onboarded.
## Underaged persons can be employed to do only "light jobs" which do not interfere with their education, health and development. There is no exhaustive definition of "hard jobs", however, for example, working outside during the winter time would be deemed as "hard work". Each fleet needs to make sure that a certified work safety and security expert confirms that the job as a courier is suitable for minors.
## In case underaged couriers would have to deliver orders containing age restricted goods, fleets would need to acquire confirmation of the the certified work safety and security expert. This aspect is not regulated, except for a blanket provision in the Employment Code that specifies that the work duties should be suitable for the proper development of the minor.
## Minors cannot work more than 6 hours/day and 30 hours/week in total.
## Minors are not allowed to work overtime or night time (i.e. between 22 and 6).
## Minors are entitled to 3 additional vacation days per year.
## Minors are entitled to a 30 minutes break if the working time exceeds 4 hours/day.

Summary and update: *Commercial Patent and Licence for Bolt's (Asunción, Paraguay)*

The municipality of Asuncion requires that businesses firstly apply for a commercial patent and then proceed with an application of a commercial licence to operate in the Municipality.

*Commercial Patent*

A Commercial Patent is an authorisation from the Municipality to operate as a business entity i.e. Bolt PY can operate in the Municipality.  It is mandatory to have only one patent per municipality, after getting the Commercial Patent a tax needs to be paid every year, it is a tax that is liquidated annually, according to the previous presentation of the assets declared before the tax authority of the closed accounting balance of the previous year.

Bolt obtained the Commercial Patent by the Asunción Municipality, this was confirmed with the department of Tax Management of the municipality, it is registered with the commercial patent No. 138514, RMC No. 857271/9 and RUC No. 80124223-1. The patent payment is up to date, including the amount due for the year 2024. Find attached the certificate of tax compliance. 

*Commercial Licence*

Commercial Licences relate to the authorisation to operate in a specific location (a property). i.e. an office, hub or a store. 

The objective is to start the application of the two Commercial Licences as soon as possible  to avoid sanctions from the Local Municipality.

Hi

Since our goal is to continue using the rented space and stay on good terms with the landlord, my advice is to start a (friendly) discussion with the landlord with the aim of agreeing to a deadline when all maintenance is complete.

The most logical option would be to negotiate a price reduction from the landlord. This may incentivize the landlord to agree to a deadline. Keep in mind that we are not in a good position to _demand_ a price reduction. This is because the agreement excludes it to a degree (section 22), but also because the landlord is not liable for the fire. Therefore we should _ask_ for the price reduction.

* The price reduction can be asked for rent already paid and also for future rent until all maintenance has been completed. The problem here is that it is more difficult to argue that the rent, which Bolt has already agreed to by paying it, should be reduced. It also less likely to be agreed by the landlord.
* The price reduction can be asked for future rent until all maintenance has been completed.
* We can offer a sort of compromise to the landlord: the price is not reduced on condition that all maintenance is completed by an agreed upon date; if that deadline passes and the warehouse is still not properly usable then the price will be reduced. This would be the softest approach and the landlord may be more likely to agree to this one.

Amount of the price reduction depends on (i) what would be the rent if the warehouse’s conditions had been like they are now from the start, (ii) but also what would be a reasonable price reduction that the landlord could agree to. I can’t provide a number here, unfortunately.

Similarly, the date to be agreed upon depends on how many work is still needed to be done and what would be a reasonable date when the work could be completed.

Keep in mind that there is still risk that landlord simply refuses to agree to the price reduction as we can’t demand this contractually. I am still not familiar with the background and aftermath of the warehouse fire and am not aware of what has been and hasn’t been covered by insurance – this may further affect our chances of getting the landlord to agree to a price reduction.

* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.

** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments
* Only successful card payments can be refunded to card.

For 🚗[ Driver: I want to delete my account|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360010217173#request-to-delete-drivers-account], *Portugal* uses a different undocumented process compared to *Global* to prevent fraud.

“🌍 *Global process:*

* Go to the driver's profile in *Admin Panel* (Rides > Partners > Edit) and change the current status to _Deleted_ and click _Save_ at the bottom.
* In *Admin* tick _GDPR:_ _Driver deletion request_ label and click _Save_
** If you don't see this label, go to [GDPR: Driver deletion label not visible in Admin|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360010217173#gdpr-driver-deletion-label-not-visible-in-admin]
* Leave a comment on the profile: _Deletion request as of (enter date) + Beehive case link_ and save the comment”

However, the process for the *Portuguese* market is:

* “Admin Driver profile > Change “Status” from “Active” to “Hidden” > Add a comment with the beehive link.
* In *Admin* tick _GDPR:_ _Driver deletion request_ label and click _Save_
** If you don't see this label, go to [GDPR: Driver deletion label not visible in Admin|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360010217173#gdpr-driver-deletion-label-not-visible-in-admin]
* Leave a comment on the profile: _Deletion request as of (enter date) + Beehive case link_ and save the comment“

 

--

So Portugal hides the Driver profile, instead of deleting the Partner profile. *Their reasoning*:

The reasoning for the different process is that we noticed a pattern where drivers ask for account deletion to clear their records (fraud, quality, safety), by creating a new partner account after with a different email/phone.

*Why the duplication with the deleted partner is not found?* We have too much deleted partners accounts (+150.000), prior to 2023 we wouldn’t copy driver accounts, instead we created new partners every time there was a fleet change.
It is impossible for us to make this cross check.

Since 2023, a driver has only 1 partner account, he cannot be separated from it, and we track all his info at partner level. If we follow the current guideline, we’ll see fraudulent, aggressive drivers being able to avoid hardblocks and even getting unblocked, as we’ve seen in the past before implementing this process.
